audits.subsystem: Payment Session Lifecycle (create -> confirm -> initiate -> settle)
audits.summary:
LIFECYCLE TRACE

SessionStatus enum (paybank-core/src/models.rs:100-109): Pending, Authorized, Processing, Completed, Expired. There is NO failed/returned/reversed terminal state for sessions — all failure paths reuse Expired.

1) CREATE (sessions.rs:12-55, session_repo.rs:7-34). create_session picks a rail via PaymentRail::choose (models.rs:16-26: >$25,000 -> Wire, else FedNow, else RTP, else ACH), sets expires_at = now()+24h (sessions.rs:26), inserts a row with status 'pending' (session_repo.rs:21). Returns a pay URL + QR. Also exposed via merchant_api.rs create_payment_link (same 24h, line 113).

2) CONFIRM (confirm.rs:20-89). Loads session; rejects if Expired or now>expires_at (line 28); short-circuits returning "completed" if already Completed (line 31). It writes customer details (HARDCODED customer@example.com / 5555555555, confirm.rs:39-40), then if account_number/routing/type already present on the session it calls create_counterparty and stores "counterparty_id|external_account_id" into column_counterparty_id (line 69), then sets status -> Authorized (line 77-83). No guard that prior status was Pending; a Processing session can be pushed back to Authorized.

3) INITIATE — TWO separate endpoints both registered:
   - POST /api/sessions/initiate (initiate.rs:13-103, JSON body session_id), and
   - POST /api/sessions/:id/initiate (sessions.rs:150-217, path id).
   Both do: reject if Expired/expired (sessions.rs:158, initiate.rs:21); return "completed" if already Completed; require rail_used and column_counterparty_id; set status -> Processing; call paybank_payments::initiate_transfer; on Ok set status -> Completed (+provider ref) and insert a transactions row; on Err set status -> Expired and return the error. They differ in reference prefix (sessions.rs:202 uses "pay_{id}", initiate.rs:82 uses "txn_{id}") and recipient-id parsing (sessions.rs:165-170 takes external_account_id when MT key present, else FIRST split; initiate.rs:37-44 same MT branch but else uses counterparty_id) — duplicated, divergent logic.

4) SETTLE (webhooks.rs). column_webhook (verified HMAC SHA256 over body, lines 30-41) maps provider status: settled/completed -> Completed, failed/returned -> Expired, anything else -> Processing (lines 54-82); session matched by parsing "Session {uuid}" out of description. moderntreasury_webhook (lines 89-137) maps settled/completed -> Completed, failed/returned/reversed -> Expired; ALSO unconditionally inserts a transactions row with merchant_id = Uuid::nil() and amount 0 and rail FedNow (lines 120-133).

EXPIRY: purely lazy/time-based. No background sweeper exists (no tokio::spawn/interval anywhere). A session past expires_at keeps status 'pending'/'authorized' in the DB until a request touches it; the in-handler checks (now>expires_at) reject it but never persist Expired. The SSE stream (sessions.rs:104-148) only breaks on Completed/Expired stored status, so an expired-by-time session never reaches those states and the loop runs until the client disconnects or get_session errors.

SSE STREAM (sessions.rs:116-141): polls get_session every 2s, emits {session_id,status,amount_cents}. No auth on the stream (any session id is streamable). Breaks only on stored Completed/Expired.

gaps.title: No idempotency / double-submit guard on initiate — duplicate money movement
gaps.detail: Neither initiate endpoint takes an idempotency key, nor does it conditionally guard the status transition. The flow is read session -> check status != Completed -> update_status(Processing) -> initiate_transfer. update_status (session_repo.rs:56-75) is an unconditional UPDATE ... SET status=$2 with no WHERE on current status, so it is not a compare-and-swap. Two concurrent POSTs (or a retry/double-click) both pass the 'not Completed' read, both set Processing, and both call paybank_payments::initiate_transfer, sending TWO transfers to the provider for one session. There are also two routes (/api/sessions/initiate and /api/sessions/:id/initiate) hitting the same session. An idempotency_keys table exists (migrations 001:141-153, models.rs:425) but is NOT used here. For a money-movement product this is a duplicate-payment defect.
gaps.fix_direction: Make the Processing transition a conditional CAS: UPDATE ... SET status='processing' WHERE id=$1 AND status IN ('authorized') RETURNING ...; only proceed to initiate_transfer if exactly one row was updated (rowcount=1). Require/propagate a provider idempotency key (keyed by session id) into initiate_transfer so the provider de-dupes. Consider collapsing the two duplicate endpoints into one.

gaps.title: Transfer/processing failure maps session to Expired, losing money-state and enabling silent retries
gaps.detail: On initiate_transfer Err the handler sets SessionStatus::Expired (sessions.rs:213, initiate.rs:96). Webhooks map provider 'failed'/'returned'/'reversed' to Expired too. SessionStatus has no Failed/Returned/Reversed state (models.rs:100-109), so a genuine transfer failure is indistinguishable from a timed-out unused link. Worse: the failure path sets Expired but the error may be ambiguous (network timeout/5xx) — the transfer may actually have been accepted by the provider while the session shows Expired, or a returned/reversed settled transfer (real money already moved) is shown identically to 'never paid'. Operators cannot tell a failed payment from an expired link, and reconciliation against the ledger is impossible. A 'reversed' webhook silently flips Completed->Expired with no compensating ledger entry.
gaps.fix_direction: Add distinct terminal states (Failed, Returned, Reversed) to SessionStatus and the DB. On initiate_transfer Err, only mark Failed when the provider definitively rejected; for ambiguous errors keep Processing and reconcile via status polling/webhook. Never reuse Expired for transfer outcomes. Treat reversed/returned as their own states with ledger reversal.

gaps.title: Modern Treasury webhook has NO signature verification — forgeable settlement
gaps.detail: moderntreasury_webhook(State, body_bytes) parses the JSON body and directly drives session status to Completed/Expired (lines 108-118) and inserts a transactions row, with zero authentication — no HMAC, no signature header, no shared-secret check (contrast column_webhook which verifies an HMAC at lines 30-41). Anyone who can POST to /api/webhooks/moderntreasury can mark any session_id 'completed' (or 'expired') by crafting remittance_information='Session {uuid}'. For the PRIMARY provider this means an attacker can forge payment settlement.
gaps.fix_direction: Verify the Modern Treasury webhook signature (X-Signature HMAC over the raw body using the MT webhook secret) before processing, mirroring column_webhook, and reject on mismatch.

gaps.title: Webhook inserts bogus transaction rows: merchant_id nil, amount 0, rail FedNow
gaps.detail: Every MT webhook with a non-empty transfer_id unconditionally inserts a transactions row with merchant_id=Uuid::nil(), amount_cents=0, rail=FedNow regardless of the real session/amount/rail, reference 'mt_{transfer_id}'. transactions.merchant_id is a NOT NULL FK to merchants(id) (migration 001:75) so the nil UUID insert will fail the FK unless a nil merchant exists — the error is swallowed by `let _ =`. Even if it succeeds it pollutes financial transaction records with zero-dollar, wrong-merchant, wrong-rail rows that corrupt reporting/balances. It also creates a SECOND transactions row in addition to the one written by the initiate handler for the same session.
gaps.fix_direction: Look up the session to populate real merchant_id, amount_cents, rail; insert at most once per session (idempotent on session_id/transfer_id) and stop fabricating placeholder values. Do not swallow the insert error.

gaps.title: No state-machine guard on transitions; update_status is an unconditional overwrite
gaps.detail: update_status always overwrites status with no check of the prior value, so illegal transitions are allowed: confirm can move Processing/Completed-adjacent sessions back to Authorized; the Column webhook 'else' branch (lines 73-81) flips a session that already settled (Completed) back to Processing on any unrecognized status string; a late 'failed' webhook can move Completed -> Expired. Combined with lazy expiry, ordering of webhook delivery determines final state with no monotonicity guarantees.
gaps.fix_direction: Encode allowed transitions (pending->authorized->processing->completed, plus failure terminals) and enforce them in the UPDATE WHERE clause; ignore backward/illegal transitions, especially never downgrade a Completed session.

gaps.title: Sessions never get persisted as Expired; expiry is lazy-only with no sweeper
gaps.location: crates/paybank-api/src/routes/sessions.rs:158, confirm.rs:28, initiate.rs:21; no background job in src/main.rs
gaps.detail: Expiry is enforced only inside request handlers by comparing now>expires_at, which returns SessionExpired but does NOT write status=Expired. There is no background sweeper (grep found no tokio::spawn/interval). Therefore time-expired sessions sit in 'pending'/'authorized' indefinitely in the DB, admin/merchant listings and the status index (migration 001:70) misreport them as live, and the SSE stream (sessions.rs:124-140) never terminates for an expired-but-untouched session because the stored status never becomes Expired/Completed (loop only breaks on those, line 134).
gaps.fix_direction: Add a periodic job to set status=Expired WHERE expires_at < now() AND status IN ('pending','authorized'); have the SSE loop also break on wall-clock expiry; persist Expired in the handler when the time check trips.

gaps.title: Two divergent initiate endpoints with different reference prefixes and recipient parsing
gaps.detail: Both /api/sessions/initiate and /api/sessions/:id/initiate are live and do nearly the same thing but diverge: (a) reference prefix differs ('pay_{id}' vs 'txn_{id}'); since transactions.reference is UNIQUE (migration 001:79) the SAME session can produce two distinct references via the two endpoints, defeating the only de-dup the schema offers and yielding two transactions for one payment. (b) Recipient id parsing differs when MT key is absent: sessions.rs:169 uses raw.split('|').next() while initiate.rs:43 uses counterparty_id (same value) but the two code paths can drift. Duplicated money-moving logic is a correctness hazard.
gaps.fix_direction: Delete one endpoint (or route both to one shared function), and use a deterministic reference derived solely from session id so retries collide on the UNIQUE constraint instead of duplicating.

gaps.title: Confirm overwrites real customer contact info with hardcoded placeholders
gaps.detail: update_customer_details is called with email='customer@example.com' and phone='5555555555' hardcoded, even though the ConfirmRequest only carries name/address. This destroys any customer_email/phone captured at session creation (CreateSessionRequest has customer_email, models.rs:306) and writes junk PII used downstream for counterparty creation and potentially compliance/KYC. For a regulated product, persisting fabricated contact data is a data-integrity/compliance issue.
gaps.fix_direction: Accept real email/phone in ConfirmRequest (or preserve existing session values via COALESCE) instead of hardcoding placeholders.

gaps.title: SSE stream and session detail endpoints have no authorization
gaps.detail: GET /api/sessions/:id, /:id/qr, /:id/stream are unauthenticated and key only on the session UUID, exposing amount, status, and (via get_session model) potentially customer fields to anyone with the id. The pay link is meant to be shareable, but full session detail/stream returning customer data without auth is a leakage risk.
gaps.fix_direction: Scope public endpoints to non-sensitive fields, or require the merchant/customer context; avoid returning customer PII on unauthenticated reads.

gaps.title: Transaction written before/independent of settlement confirmation
gaps.detail: On a successful initiate_transfer (transfer merely accepted/submitted by provider, not settled) the handler immediately sets status=Completed and inserts a transactions row with settled_at=now(). The actual settlement comes later via webhook. So 'Completed' and a settled transaction are recorded at submission time, overstating settlement and conflicting with a later failed/returned webhook (which then maps to Expired but leaves the transactions row in place).
gaps.fix_direction: Distinguish 'submitted/processing' from 'settled'; only set Completed and write the settlement transaction on the settlement webhook, and reverse/flag the transaction on returned/reversed.

gaps.title: generate_qr_data is a no-op with dead branches
gaps.detail: Both branches return pay_url.to_string(); the prefix check and 'https://pay.noor.com/p/' constant are dead code. Cosmetic, but indicates incomplete QR/deep-link handling.
gaps.fix_direction: Remove dead branches or implement the intended canonical pay-link format.

risks: READ-ONLY audit; no files were modified. Findings are from static reading of source and migrations; runtime behavior (e.g., whether a nil-merchant row exists for the webhook insert) was not executed.
Could not confirm whether any reverse proxy/middleware adds auth in front of public session endpoints; router.rs shows none.

Did not exhaustively read column.rs/moderntreasury.rs provider clients for whether initiate_transfer passes a provider-side idempotency key; lib.rs initiate_transfer signature shows none is threaded through.

audits.subsystem: Modern Treasury integration (counterparty + payment-order creation, status polling)
audits.summary:
Modern Treasury (MT) is the primary payment provider, selected at runtime by PaymentProvider::primary() (crates/paybank-payments/src/lib.rs:18-27) when MODERN_TREASURY_API_KEY, MODERN_TREASURY_ORG_ID and MT_INTERNAL_ACCOUNT_ID env vars are all set; otherwise it falls back to Column.

CLIENT/CONFIG (moderntreasury.rs:11-36): mt_client() builds a fresh reqwest::Client on every call. Base URL is hardcoded to https://app.moderntreasury.com/api (line 9) — production only, no sandbox/env switch. Auth is HTTP Basic with org_id:api_key base64-encoded; the header is marked sensitive (line 26). A single 15s total request timeout is set (line 18); no connect timeout, no retry policy, no backoff. The internal originating account is read from MT_INTERNAL_ACCOUNT_ID (lib.rs:75-76).

COUNTERPARTY CREATION (create_counterparty, moderntreasury.rs:97-149): POSTs /counterparties with the customer name plus one external account (account_details {type, account_number} and routing_details {routing_number, routing_number_type:"aba"}). Routing type is always hardcoded "aba" (line 112). On non-2xx it logs a warning and returns ModernTreasuryError with the body. On success it parses CounterpartyResponse and returns (counterparty_id, first_account_id); if accounts is empty it falls back to using the counterparty id as the account id (lines 139-141). The (cp_id|ext_id) pair is stored joined by "|" in session.column_counterparty_id (confirm.rs:69-71).

PAYMENT-ORDER CREATION (create_transfer, moderntreasury.rs:151-204): POSTs /payment_orders with type derived from rail (ach/wire; Rtp and FedNow both map to "rtp", lines 160-164), amount (i64 cents), direction hardcoded "credit", originating_account_id = MT_INTERNAL_ACCOUNT_ID, receiving_account_id = the recipient id chosen in the route, receiving_account_type hardcoded "external_account", currency hardcoded "USD". On non-2xx it logs and returns an error; on success parses PaymentOrderResponse {id, status}. NO Idempotency-Key header is ever sent to MT on either counterparty or payment-order creation.

CALLERS/ORCHESTRATION: initiate_transfer (lib.rs:65-107) wraps create_transfer. It is invoked from two HTTP routes: routes/initiate.rs:54 (POST /api/sessions/initiate) and routes/sessions.rs:174 (POST /api/sessions/:id/initiate). Both set the session to Processing, call MT, and on success set Completed + insert a transaction row; on error they set status to Expired and propagate. update_status (session_repo.rs:56-75) is an unconditional UPDATE ... WHERE id=$1 with no compare-and-swap on the previous status, and the routes are mounted with no idempotency middleware (router.rs:76-83), despite a full idempotency_keys table/repo existing in the codebase but being unused on these paths.

STATUS POLLING (get_transfer_status, moderntreasury.rs:206-223): GET /payment_orders/{id} but does NOT check resp.status() before parsing JSON — a 4xx/5xx error body is fed straight to PaymentOrderResponse::deserialize. get_payment_order_details and get_counterparty_details (lines 225-265) do check status first and return raw serde_json::Value; these back the read-only GET /api/mt/* admin endpoints (mt.rs).

gaps.title: No Idempotency-Key sent to Modern Treasury on payment-order creation — retries/replays can double-pay
gaps.detail: MT supports and recommends an Idempotency-Key header to make POST /payment_orders safe against retries. The code sends none. Combined with a single fresh reqwest client and no retry/backoff, any transport-level retry by the caller, a client/proxy retry, or a duplicate user request will create a SECOND payment order and move money twice. There is no MT-side dedupe to catch it.
gaps.fix_direction: Generate a stable idempotency key per logical payment (e.g. derived from session_id) and pass it as the `Idempotency-Key` header on both /payment_orders and /counterparties POSTs. Persist the key so retries reuse it.

gaps.title: Transfer initiation is not guarded by an atomic state transition — concurrent/duplicate requests double-pay
gaps.detail: initiate_payment (sessions.rs) reads the session, then unconditionally sets status=Processing and calls MT. It does not even check for an existing Completed/Processing status before firing (initiate.rs at least checks Completed at line 24, but still races). update_status uses WHERE id=$1 with no compare-and-swap, so two concurrent POSTs to /api/sessions/:id/initiate both pass the read, both set Processing, and both call create_transfer — two MT payment orders, two debits. The unused idempotency_keys table is not applied to these routes (router.rs:76-83).
gaps.fix_direction: Make the Processing transition a conditional UPDATE (WHERE id=$1 AND status IN ('authorized')) and only call MT if exactly one row was updated; or apply the existing idempotency middleware to these routes. Send an MT idempotency key as defense in depth.

gaps.title: On MT error after the order may have been created, status is set to Expired and money state is lost
gaps.detail: If create_transfer returns Err for ANY reason — including a 15s timeout, a connection reset, or a non-2xx body — the route sets the session to Expired and returns the error. But MT may have actually accepted and created the payment order (timeout/network errors are ambiguous; the order can be in-flight at MT). The provider_transfer_id is never captured, no transaction row is written, and the session looks dead. This both silently drops a real in-flight payment and invites the operator/user to retry, producing a duplicate (compounds the double-pay risk above).
gaps.fix_direction: Distinguish definite failures from ambiguous ones (timeout, 5xx, connection error). For ambiguous outcomes, mark the session as needing reconciliation rather than Expired, and reconcile against MT using the idempotency key / by listing payment orders before any retry.

gaps.title: get_transfer_status parses JSON without checking HTTP status — silently turns error bodies into bogus status / drops failures
gaps.detail: Unlike the other GET helpers, get_transfer_status (used by check_transfer_status, lib.rs:120) never calls resp.status().is_success(). A 401/404/429/5xx returns an error JSON body that fails to deserialize into PaymentOrderResponse, surfacing as a generic 'Failed to parse payment order status' error that masks the real HTTP cause (auth failure, rate limit, not found). Worse, if MT ever returns a 200 with a partial body lacking `status`, behavior is undefined. Status reconciliation can thus silently fail.
gaps.fix_direction: Check resp.status().is_success() and surface status+body like the other helpers do before deserializing; treat 404 vs 429 vs 5xx distinctly for retry/reconcile logic.

gaps.title: FedNow rail silently downgraded to RTP, and all routing details hardcoded as ACH 'aba'
gaps.detail: PaymentRail::FedNow is mapped to order_type "rtp" (line 163), so a FedNow-intended payment is sent over a different network without any signal. Separately, every counterparty's routing_number_type is hardcoded "aba" (line 112), which is the ACH routing convention; for wire/RTP this may be the wrong routing identifier type and could cause MT to reject or misroute. Both are silent semantic changes to money movement.
gaps.fix_direction: Map FedNow to its correct MT order type (or reject if unsupported) and derive routing_number_type from the rail/identifier rather than hardcoding 'aba'.

gaps.title: Empty MT accounts array falls back to using counterparty id as the receiving account id
gaps.detail: On a partial counterparty response with no accounts, external_account_id silently becomes the counterparty id. That id is later stored and (for MT) passed as receiving_account_id with receiving_account_type="external_account" (lib.rs:77-84, initiate.rs:40-44). Passing a counterparty id where an external_account id is expected will at best be rejected by MT and at worst misroute; either way the partial response is masked instead of surfaced as an error.
gaps.fix_direction: Treat a counterparty response with no usable external account as a hard error rather than substituting the counterparty id.

gaps.title: MT base URL hardcoded to production; no sandbox/env separation
gaps.detail: MT_BASE_URL is a const pointing at app.moderntreasury.com. There is no environment switch, so tests/staging cannot target a sandbox and any non-prod run hits live MT (real money) if creds are present.
gaps.fix_direction: Make the base URL configurable via env with a safe default and assert it matches the credential environment.

risks: READ-ONLY audit: no files were modified.
I did not locate any MT sandbox/test config, so the 'production-only base URL' finding assumes no override exists elsewhere; confirm before remediation.

Whether a duplicate POST to /api/sessions/:id/initiate is reachable depends on auth/session gating not fully traced here, but no status guard or idempotency layer exists on the route, so the double-pay path is open by code as written.

audits.summary:
Provider selection is purely an env-var gate, not a runtime fallback. `PaymentProvider::primary()` (crates/paybank-payments/src/lib.rs:18-27) returns ModernTreasury IFF all three of MODERN_TREASURY_API_KEY, MODERN_TREASURY_ORG_ID and MT_INTERNAL_ACCOUNT_ID are set; otherwise it returns Column. There is no logic that tries Modern Treasury first and "falls back" to Column on failure — despite the README/task framing of Column as a fallback. Both `create_counterparty` (lib.rs:35-63) and `initiate_transfer` (lib.rs:65-107) match on `primary()` and dispatch to exactly one provider. If MT fails, the error (AppError::ModernTreasuryError) propagates to the caller and the session is marked Expired (sessions.rs:213, initiate.rs:93); Column is never attempted. So the Column path is only reachable in an environment where MT env vars are absent — i.e. it is an either/or deployment toggle, not a resilience fallback.

Rail selection: `PaymentRail::choose(supports_fednow, supports_rtp, amount_cents)` in crates/paybank-core/src/models.rs:16-26 — amount > $25,000 (2_500_000 cents) => Wire, else FedNow if supported, else RTP if supported, else ACH. The `supports_wire` flag is accepted by `rail::choose_rail` (rail.rs:3-10) but ignored (param prefixed `_`), and `choose_rail` itself appears unused — callers (sessions.rs:20, merchant_api.rs:112) call `PaymentRail::choose` directly. Rail is chosen once at session creation and stored as `rail_used`; it is re-read at transfer time, so the original choice (made before the amount or bank capabilities could change) is the one used.

Transfer endpoints per rail: Column's `create_transfer` (column.rs:142-189) always POSTs to a single `/transfers` endpoint and encodes the rail in a `type` field ("ach"/"wire"/"rtp"/"fednow"). Note `PaymentRail::column_endpoint()` (models.rs:28-34) defines per-rail paths ("/transfers/ach", "/transfers/realtime", "/transfers/wire") but is dead code — never called by column.rs. Modern Treasury's `create_transfer` (moderntreasury.rs:151-204) POSTs to `/payment_orders` with `type` = "ach"/"wire"/"rtp", collapsing both Rtp and FedNow to "rtp". Status checks: lib.rs:115-123 `check_transfer_status` dispatches on a provider string ("modern_treasury" | "column"); Column GET `/transfers/{id}` (column.rs:191-211), MT GET `/payment_orders/{id}` (moderntreasury.rs:206-223).

Error handling: Column wraps everything in AppError::ColumnError -> HTTP 502 (error.rs:78). create_transfer checks HTTP status before parsing (column.rs:172-180), but create_counterparty (column.rs:106-139) and get_transfer_status (column.rs:191-211) do NOT check resp.status() — they call .json() directly, so an HTTP 4xx/5xx error body is treated as a parse attempt and surfaced as a misleading "Failed to parse" error. Webhooks: Column webhook (webhooks.rs:17-87) verifies an HMAC-SHA256 signature against WEBHOOK_SECRET; the Modern Treasury webhook (webhooks.rs:89-137) performs NO signature verification at all and will act on any unauthenticated POST.

Testing: There are zero tests anywhere in the workspace — no tests/ dirs, no #[cfg(test)]/#[test]/#[tokio::test] in any crate. The Column fallback path (and rail selection) is entirely untested.

gaps.title: "Fallback" provider is not a fallback — no failover on Modern Treasury failure
gaps.detail: PaymentProvider::primary() is a static env-var toggle. initiate_transfer/create_counterparty dispatch to exactly one provider; if Modern Treasury returns an error it propagates and the session is marked Expired (sessions.rs:213, initiate.rs:93). Column is never tried as a fallback. The system is documented/positioned as MT-primary with Column-fallback for resilience, but in code it is an either/or deployment toggle. In a money-movement product this means a transient MT outage fails customer payments with no automatic alternate rail/provider, contrary to the stated design.
gaps.fix_direction: Decide intent: if true failover is required, wrap the MT attempt and on retryable errors attempt Column with the same idempotency context; ensure the persisted provider string reflects which one actually executed. If it is intentionally a toggle, rename/redocument so operators don't assume failover.

gaps.title: Persisted provider for status/webhook reconciliation is wrong when Column is active
gaps.detail: initiate_transfer returns TransferResult.provider ("modern_treasury" or "column"), but the session/transaction write path (sessions.rs, initiate.rs) only stores the provider_transfer_id via update_status/create_transaction — the provider string is discarded. There is no provider column populated on the transaction, and merchant_api.rs:66 hardcodes "provider":"moderntreasury" for every listed payment. check_transfer_status(provider, id) requires the correct provider string to pick the right API; with the provider not persisted there is no reliable way to reconcile a Column transfer's status later, and the MT GET endpoint would be hit for a Column transfer id. For a regulated ledger this breaks settlement reconciliation when Column is the active provider.
gaps.fix_direction: Persist transfer.provider on the session/transaction record and use it when calling check_transfer_status; remove the hardcoded "moderntreasury" literal in list_payments and read the stored provider.

gaps.title: Modern Treasury webhook has no signature verification
gaps.detail: moderntreasury_webhook accepts a raw body and acts on it (updating session status to Completed/Expired and creating transactions) with zero authentication — no HMAC/signature check, unlike column_webhook (webhooks.rs:30-41) which verifies an HMAC-SHA256. An attacker who can reach the endpoint can forge a payment_order.settled event for any session id (embedded in remittance_information) and drive a session to Completed, marking unsettled money as settled. This is a critical money-safety/forgery hole. (Cross-provider inconsistency: Column path is protected, MT path is not.)
gaps.fix_direction: Verify Modern Treasury webhook signatures (X-Signature HMAC over raw body using the MT webhook key) before processing, mirroring the Column handler; reject on mismatch.

gaps.title: Column create_counterparty and get_transfer_status do not check HTTP status before parsing
gaps.detail: Unlike create_transfer (column.rs:172-180) and the MT equivalents (moderntreasury.rs:124-132,184-195,232-238), create_counterparty's entity and account calls and get_transfer_status call resp.json() directly without checking resp.status().is_success(). On an HTTP 4xx/5xx the error JSON body fails to deserialize into EntityResponse/AccountResponse/TransferStatusResponse and surfaces as a misleading "Failed to parse ..." error, masking the real provider error (e.g. auth failure, validation). A failed counterparty creation could also be misreported, and a failed status poll could mis-drive reconciliation.
gaps.fix_direction: Add resp.status().is_success() checks that read and surface the body, consistent with create_transfer and the MT functions, before deserializing.

gaps.title: Column counterparty uses hardcoded placeholder address; real customer address ignored
gaps.detail: When the Column provider is active, create_counterparty in lib.rs constructs a CustomerAddress hardcoded to "123 Main St / New York / NY / 10001 / US" regardless of the real customer address that confirm.rs collected (req.customer_address_line_1/city/state/postal_code/country) and stored. The real address is persisted to the session but never passed into the Column entity. The MT path takes a different shape entirely (no address). For a KYC/regulated entity creation this submits false address data to the bank partner.
gaps.fix_direction: Thread the real customer address through create_counterparty into the Column CustomerAddress instead of the hardcoded literal.

gaps.title: FedNow rail is silently downgraded to RTP on Modern Treasury, but sent as fednow on Column
gaps.detail: PaymentRail::choose can select FedNow. MT's create_transfer maps both Rtp and FedNow to order_type "rtp" (moderntreasury.rs:163), while Column maps FedNow to "fednow" (column.rs:161). The same logical rail produces different actual rails depending on which provider is active, with no record of the substitution. RTP and FedNow have different network availability, limits, and settlement semantics; a session stored as rail_used=fednow could actually be sent over RTP. This is a correctness/disclosure inconsistency between the two providers.
gaps.fix_direction: Make rail handling explicit and consistent: if MT cannot do FedNow, either choose RTP up front or record the actual rail used; align the two providers' rail->type maps or document the divergence.

gaps.title: Dead/unused rail abstractions create false confidence (column_endpoint, choose_rail supports_wire)
gaps.detail: PaymentRail::column_endpoint() returns per-rail paths (/transfers/ach, /transfers/realtime, /transfers/wire) but Column actually posts to a single /transfers endpoint (column.rs:166) and column_endpoint is never called. rail::choose_rail takes supports_wire but ignores it (param _supports_wire) and is itself unused (callers use PaymentRail::choose directly). These suggest an intended design that was never wired up, and could mislead a maintainer into thinking rail-specific endpoints or wire-capability checks are in effect.
gaps.fix_direction: Either remove the dead code or wire it up; if Column truly requires per-rail endpoints, use column_endpoint() in create_transfer.

gaps.title: No tests anywhere; Column path and rail selection completely unverified
gaps.detail: There are no test files or inline #[test]/#[tokio::test]/#[cfg(test)] modules in the entire workspace. PaymentRail::choose boundary behavior (e.g. exactly 2_500_000 vs 2_500_001), provider selection, and the Column request/response shapes are untested. For a regulated money-movement product the absence of even unit tests on rail selection thresholds and provider dispatch is a significant gap.
gaps.fix_direction: Add unit tests for PaymentRail::choose boundaries and PaymentProvider::primary() env gating, and contract/mocked-HTTP tests for the Column and MT request/response (de)serialization.

gaps.title: Column transfer request field shape likely does not match Column's real API
gaps.detail: CreateTransferRequest sends merchant_account_id/counterparty_id/amount_cents/currency/description/type to POST /transfers. Column's real API uses distinct endpoints and field names per transfer type (e.g. ach_transfers with counterparty_id, amount, currency_code). The entity/account creation flow (column.rs:88-140) and TransferResponse{id,status} are similarly speculative. Combined with the missing HTTP-status checks, a real Column deployment would likely fail at runtime with the misleading parse errors noted above. This reinforces that the fallback path is unexercised.
gaps.fix_direction: Validate request/response schemas against the current Column API docs and add integration tests against Column sandbox before relying on this path.

risks: Column is the active provider only when MT env vars are unset; in the primary (MT-configured) deployment the entire Column code path never executes, so bugs in it are latent and would surface only on a config change.

I did not have a running Column sandbox to confirm the actual API contract; the request/response struct mismatches are inferred from Column's public API conventions, not verified against a live response.

Idempotency: neither provider's transfer call sends an idempotency key to the provider; retries (or a future failover) could double-submit transfers. This is outside the strict Column scope but directly affects money-safety of the transfer path.

audits.subsystem: Plaid bank linking (link-token create, public-token exchange, auth/get, account flow into session)
audits.summary:
End-to-end flow for Plaid bank linking in Depost:

1) Link-token creation. The customer-facing client calls GET /api/plaid/link-token?session_id=<uuid> (router.rs:93). The handler `create_link_token` (crates/paybank-api/src/routes/plaid.rs:15-21) ignores AppState (`State(_state)`), reads the session_id from the query string, and calls `paybank_payments::create_link_token` (plaid.rs:123-153). That builds a LinkTokenCreateRequest with client_name "Depost", country_codes ["US"], language "en", products ["auth"], and user.client_user_id = session_id.to_string(), then POSTs to {PLAID_BASE_URL}/link/token/create. PLAID_CLIENT_ID and PLAID_SECRET come from env (plaid.rs:14-20). The link_token is returned as JSON to the browser, which opens Plaid Link.

2) Public-token exchange + auth. After the user finishes Plaid Link, the browser POSTs JSON {session_id, public_token} to POST /api/plaid/exchange (router.rs:94). Handler `exchange_public_token` (routes/plaid.rs:29-58) calls `paybank_payments::exchange_public_token` (plaid.rs:155-182), which POSTs {client_id, secret, public_token} to /item/public_token/exchange and returns the long-lived `access_token`. The handler immediately calls `get_auth(&access_token)` (plaid.rs:184-234), which POSTs to /auth/get and parses accounts + numbers.ach. get_auth builds a HashMap of ACH numbers keyed by account_id, then for each account produces a BankAccountDetails containing the raw account_number, routing_number, balances, etc. (plaid.rs:206-233). Note both account_type and subtype are set from the Plaid `subtype` field, defaulting to "checking" when absent (plaid.rs:218,224-225) — the real Plaid `type` field is parsed but discarded (account_type marked dead_code, plaid.rs:84).

3) Flow into the session. Back in the handler (routes/plaid.rs:36-53), only the FIRST account (`accounts.first()`) is persisted. It calls session_repo::update_customer_details with the account_number, routing_number, account_type, and country_code "US", passing empty strings ("") for name/email/phone/address fields. That UPDATE (session_repo.rs:129-163) writes customer_account_number, customer_routing_number, customer_account_type onto the payment_sessions row. The full accounts list (with raw numbers) is also returned in the HTTP JSON response to the browser (routes/plaid.rs:55-57).

The access_token is never persisted anywhere — it is used transiently inside the single exchange request and dropped, so item re-auth / balance refresh is impossible later.

gaps.title: Raw bank account & routing numbers stored in plaintext
gaps.detail: get_auth returns the raw account_number and routing_number (plaid.rs:222-223), and update_customer_details writes them into payment_sessions.customer_account_number / customer_routing_number which are declared as bare TEXT in migrations/001_initial_schema.sql:60-61 — no encryption, tokenization, or pgcrypto. Full bank account + routing pairs in cleartext are highly sensitive (ACH-fraud / NACHA-grade data) and a regulated money-movement product must not store them unencrypted. They are additionally echoed back to the browser in the JSON response (routes/plaid.rs:55-57).
gaps.fix_direction: Tokenize/vault the account+routing (or store a Plaid processor_token / access_token reference instead of raw PANs), encrypt at rest (pgcrypto/app-layer envelope encryption + KMS), and never return raw numbers to the client; return only masked last-4.

gaps.title: Plaid endpoints have no authentication or authorization
gaps.detail: /api/plaid/link-token and /api/plaid/exchange (router.rs:93-94) are registered with no auth layer — router.rs has no .layer/middleware/from_fn auth at all. Anyone who knows or guesses a session_id (a UUID passed in the query/body) can create a link token for it and, more dangerously, POST an arbitrary public_token to /api/plaid/exchange and overwrite that session's bank account/routing/customer fields. There is no check that the caller owns the session, and update_customer_details unconditionally overwrites the row.
gaps.fix_direction: Bind the link/exchange flow to an authenticated session secret/nonce (not just the predictable session UUID), verify the caller is authorized for that session before mutating it, and add auth middleware to the /api/plaid/* routes.

gaps.title: Hardcoded sandbox base URL; PLAID_ENV is documented but unused
gaps.detail: PLAID_BASE_URL is a const pinned to https://sandbox.plaid.com (plaid.rs:5) used for all three calls (plaid.rs:140,166,195). .env.example:16 defines PLAID_ENV="sandbox", but grep shows PLAID_ENV is read nowhere in the codebase. This means production/development environments can never be selected; deploying to prod would silently keep hitting sandbox (links to fake data, real money flows built on sandbox auth), and the operator-facing env var gives a false sense of configurability.
gaps.fix_direction: Read PLAID_ENV at startup and map sandbox/development/production to the correct base URL (https://sandbox|development|production.plaid.com); fail fast on unknown values.

gaps.title: HTTP status from Plaid is never checked before JSON parse
gaps.detail: None of create_link_token/exchange_public_token/get_auth call .error_for_status() (confirmed: no status/error_for_status in plaid.rs). On a Plaid error (e.g. invalid public_token, INVALID_CREDENTIALS, rate limit), Plaid returns 4xx/5xx with a JSON error body. The code goes straight to resp.json::<SuccessType>() (plaid.rs:146-149,172-175,201-204), which fails deserialization and surfaces a generic 'failed to parse' PlaidError, discarding Plaid's error_code/error_type/error_message. Operators and money-movement debugging lose the actual failure reason.
gaps.fix_direction: Call .error_for_status() (or inspect resp.status()) and on non-2xx deserialize Plaid's error envelope (error_code/error_type/error_message/request_id) and propagate it; only deserialize the success type on 2xx.

gaps.title: exchange handler swallows DB write failure and partial-account loss
gaps.detail: The persistence call is `let _ = session_repo::update_customer_details(...).await;` (routes/plaid.rs:37-52) — the Result is discarded, so if the UPDATE fails the API still returns 200 with accounts, leaving the session with no bank details while the client believes linking succeeded. Also only accounts.first() is stored (routes/plaid.rs:36); if the linked item has multiple accounts the user's actual selection is ignored and the first arbitrary account silently wins.
gaps.fix_direction: Propagate the DB error (?), and require the client to specify which account_id to persist rather than blindly taking the first.

gaps.title: account_type derived from subtype; real Plaid account type discarded
gaps.detail: BankAccountDetails.account_type and .subtype are both set from the Plaid `subtype` field, defaulting to 'checking' when null (plaid.rs:218,224-225). The genuine Plaid `type` field (depository/credit/etc.) is parsed but marked dead_code (plaid.rs:83-85) and never used. A non-checking subtype (e.g. 'savings') is at least preserved, but a missing subtype is silently coerced to 'checking', which then drives customer_account_type used for ACH — an incorrect account type can cause ACH returns.
gaps.fix_direction: Persist the real account type and avoid defaulting subtype to 'checking'; reject/flag accounts whose type isn't a valid ACH-eligible depository account.

gaps.title: Access token is logged-adjacent and never stored; raw numbers in info logs risk
gaps.detail: exchange_public_token logs the item_id (plaid.rs:177-180) which is acceptable, but the access_token is obtained and then dropped (never persisted), so any later need to refresh balances/auth requires re-linking. More importantly the BankAccountDetails struct (with raw account/routing) flows through handlers and is serialized to the response; if request/response logging is enabled upstream these PANs could land in logs.
gaps.fix_direction: Decide whether to securely vault the access_token for future use; ensure account/routing are never serialized to logs or unauthenticated responses.

risks: Plaintext storage of bank account + routing numbers in payment_sessions is a likely compliance violation (PCI-adjacent / GLBA / NACHA data-protection) for a regulated money-movement product.
Unauthenticated /api/plaid/exchange lets an attacker overwrite any session's banking details by guessing a session UUID, enabling account-takeover-style misdirection of funds.
All Plaid traffic is pinned to sandbox; a production deploy would operate against fake data while the system believes it is linking real accounts.

audits.subsystem: AUTH & SECURITY surface (axum API authorization, CORS, input validation, rate limiting, secrets)
audits.summary:
The Depost API router (crates/paybank-api/src/router.rs:71-112) wires ~30 routes onto a single axum Router with NO middleware whatsoever: no auth/authorization layer, no CORS layer, no rate limiting, no request-size or body limits, no tower auth extractor. main.rs (src/main.rs:23-31) builds the router and serves it directly on BIND_ADDR=0.0.0.0:8888 — every route is reachable by any unauthenticated caller on the network.

Authorization story per surface:

ADMIN surface — /api/admin/* (router.rs:99-106) plus the /admin SPA (router.rs:107-109): stats, list/get sessions, list/create/get/update merchants, banks, settlements, webhooks. NONE of these handlers (crates/paybank-api/src/routes/admin.rs, all handlers) check any credential — no session, no admin token, no header. They take only State + Query/Path/Json. Anyone who can reach the host can read every merchant, every session, every settlement, every webhook event, and CREATE/UPDATE merchants. The admin SPA itself has no login flow at all (admin/src/lib/api.ts:123-131 issues plain fetch() with only Content-Type, no Authorization header, no credentials), confirming auth was never built. Worse, admin merchant endpoints serialize the full Merchant struct via serde_json::to_value(merchant) (admin.rs:102,116,136), and admin_repo::create_merchant/get_merchant/update_merchant RETURN password_hash and api_key columns (crates/paybank-db/src/admin_repo.rs:176,199,232,299; Merchant model fields password_hash + api_key at crates/paybank-core/src/models.rs:155-156) — so these unauthenticated endpoints leak every merchant's password_hash and API key.

MERCHANT surface — /api/merchant-api/* (router.rs:88-92): balances, profile, payments, payments/timeseries, payment_links. Merchants have an api_key (models.rs:156, migration unique index idx_merchants_api_key in migrations/001_initial_schema.sql:26), but it is NEVER validated anywhere. grep for api_key/Authorization/Bearer/x-api-key across crates shows the key is only generated (admin.rs:109), stored (admin_repo), and used outbound to providers — never checked on an inbound request. Instead every merchant-api handler HARDCODES DEMO_MERCHANT_ID = 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001 (merchant_api.rs:11,51,104). So any anonymous caller can create real payment links / payment sessions (create_payment_link, merchant_api.rs:100-137 calls session_repo::create_session) and read the demo merchant's data; there is no tenant isolation and no concept of "which merchant is calling."

CUSTOMER surface — /api/sessions/*, /api/sessions/initiate, /confirm, /api/plaid/*, /pay/:id, /invoice/:id (router.rs:75-96): all unauthenticated and effectively IDOR-by-design. Knowing a session UUID lets anyone GET full session detail (sessions.rs:77-86 returns PaymentSession), stream it (SSE), and — critically — TRIGGER MONEY MOVEMENT: /api/sessions/:id/initiate (sessions.rs:150-217) and /api/sessions/initiate (initiate.rs:13-103) call paybank_payments::initiate_transfer for any session that has a counterparty linked, with no caller authentication and no authorization that the caller owns the session. list_sessions / list_transactions (sessions.rs:64, transactions.rs:24) and merchant payments take merchant_id straight from the query string with no check that the caller owns it — full cross-merchant data read by changing a query param. /api/plaid/exchange (plaid.rs:29-53) accepts session_id + public_token and writes bank account/routing numbers onto any session UUID supplied.

PROVIDER PASS-THROUGH — /api/mt/payment-orders/:id and /api/mt/counterparties/:id (router.rs:97-98, mt.rs): unauthenticated proxies that fetch arbitrary Modern Treasury payment-order and counterparty objects by ID using the server's MT credentials. Anyone can read MT objects (PII, bank details) by guessing/enumerating IDs.

WEBHOOK surface — /api/webhooks/column and /api/webhooks/moderntreasury (router.rs:86-87): Column webhook (webhooks.rs:17-87) DOES verify an HMAC-SHA256 signature against WEBHOOK_SECRET — but the comparison uses != on hex strings (webhooks.rs:35), i.e. non-constant-time, timing-attackable, and the body is parsed only after verification (good). The Modern Treasury webhook (webhooks.rs:89-137) has NO signature verification at all — it parses the body and will mark sessions Completed/Expired and CREATE transaction rows purely on attacker-controlled JSON. Since MT is the PRIMARY provider, an unauthenticated attacker can POST a forged MT webhook with remittance_information "Session <uuid>" and status "settled" to flip any session to Completed (money-state forgery / fake settlement).

CORS: none configured (only tower_http ServeDir is imported, router.rs:8; no CorsLayer). Browser same-origin protects some, but the admin SPA is served same-origin from /admin so a malicious page cannot directly read cross-origin — however because there is zero server-side auth, CORS is moot; the real exposure is direct/server-side requests and the 0.0.0.0 bind.

Input validation: minimal. Pagination is clamped (.min(200)) in admin/sessions but merchant_api list_payments does not clamp limit and computes offset = page*limit with no bounds (merchant_api.rs:52-53). Amounts (CreateSessionRequest.amount_cents, create_payment_link.amount: i64) are never validated as positive/within bounds despite AppError::InvalidAmount existing (error.rs:6) — negative or huge amounts flow into session/transfer creation. Several handlers .unwrap()/.parse().unwrap() on values (e.g. DEMO_MERCHANT_ID.parse().unwrap() merchant_api.rs:51,104; serde_json::to_value(...).unwrap() throughout admin.rs).

Secrets handling: .env (NOT in git per .gitignore line 1, and not tracked — confirmed via git ls-files) sits on disk at /home/omar/noorpay/.env containing REAL-LOOKING live-ish provider credentials: Modern Treasury org id + API key, Column API key + account id, Plaid client id + secret, DB password, and WEBHOOK_SECRET=***REMOVED*** (a 32-hex value, low entropy/looks like an MD5-style constant). These are loaded via dotenvy (main.rs:10). Provider keys are read ad hoc with std::env::var at call time (moderntreasury.rs:14, column.rs:12) rather than validated at startup.

Error handling: AppError::Database and ::Internal are masked to generic messages (error.rs:83-90, good), but ColumnError/ModernTreasuryError/PlaidError/AuthError/TemplateError return the raw upstream error string to the client (error.rs:78-81,91), which can leak provider internals.

admin_handler (router.rs:30-69) builds a filesystem path from the URL via strip_prefix("/admin") and serves admin/dist/{clean}; the [1..] slicing and lack of canonicalization is a path-traversal smell, though axum normalizes most ../ — worth flagging for review.

Net: this is an entirely open money-movement API. The single most dangerous combination is (a) unauthenticated initiate endpoints that move money and (b) an unverified Modern Treasury webhook that forges settlement, plus (c) unauthenticated admin endpoints that leak password_hash + api_key for every merchant.

gaps.title: Entire /api/admin/* surface is unauthenticated
gaps.detail: Every admin route (stats, sessions, merchants list/get/create/update, banks, settlements, webhooks) is wired with no auth middleware and no per-handler credential check. Any caller reaching the host can read all platform data and create/modify merchants. The admin SPA has no login (admin/src/lib/api.ts:123-131 uses bare fetch with no Authorization).
gaps.fix_direction: Introduce an admin authentication layer (session cookie or signed admin JWT) enforced as an axum middleware/route-layer over a nested /api/admin router; require it on every admin route and the /admin SPA. Add server-side authz, not just SPA-side gating.

gaps.title: Admin merchant endpoints leak password_hash and api_key
gaps.detail: list/get/create/update merchant serialize the full Merchant struct, and the SQL RETURNING/SELECT includes password_hash and api_key. Combined with the unauthenticated admin surface, every merchant's password hash and live API key are exposed to anyone.
gaps.fix_direction: Return a redacted DTO (MerchantResponse without password_hash; omit or mask api_key except at creation time). Never select password_hash into a serializable response struct used by JSON endpoints.

gaps.title: Modern Treasury webhook has no signature verification (settlement forgery)
gaps.detail: moderntreasury_webhook parses attacker-supplied JSON with zero authentication and will flip a session to Completed/Expired and insert transaction rows based on remittance_information 'Session <uuid>' + status. MT is the primary rail, so anyone can forge a 'settled' event to mark payments complete.
gaps.fix_direction: Verify the Modern Treasury webhook HMAC signature against a configured secret before processing, mirroring (a corrected version of) the Column path; reject on missing/invalid signature.

gaps.title: merchant api_key is never validated; merchant-api hardcodes DEMO_MERCHANT_ID
gaps.detail: Merchants have an api_key column (models.rs:156) and unique index, but no inbound request anywhere validates it (confirmed by grep). All /api/merchant-api/* handlers ignore the caller identity and operate as the hardcoded demo merchant, including create_payment_link which creates real payment sessions. No tenant isolation exists.
gaps.fix_direction: Add an API-key auth extractor (e.g. Authorization: Bearer <api_key> hashed-lookup against merchants.api_key, constant-time) that resolves the authenticated merchant_id; replace all DEMO_MERCHANT_ID usages with the authenticated id and scope queries to it.

gaps.title: Unauthenticated money-movement: /api/sessions/:id/initiate and /api/sessions/initiate
gaps.detail: Both endpoints call paybank_payments::initiate_transfer for any session UUID that has a linked counterparty, with no authentication and no check that the caller owns/authorized the session. Anyone with a session id can trigger a real transfer.
gaps.fix_direction: Require authenticated session ownership (customer session token issued at /pay load, or merchant auth) before initiating transfers; bind initiation to a one-time confirmation token rather than just the session UUID.

gaps.title: IDOR on session/transaction/merchant reads via UUID or query param
gaps.detail: get_session returns full PaymentSession to anyone with the id; list_sessions and list_transactions take merchant_id directly from the query string with no ownership check, allowing cross-merchant enumeration of sessions and transactions. get_balance (merchant_api.rs:21-31) takes merchant_id from path with no check (currently returns zeros but pattern is unsafe).
gaps.fix_direction: Derive merchant_id from authenticated credentials, not from client-supplied query/path; scope all list/get queries to the authenticated principal; consider not returning full session PII to unauthenticated callers.

gaps.title: Modern Treasury pass-through proxies expose arbitrary provider objects
gaps.detail: /api/mt/payment-orders/:id and /api/mt/counterparties/:id are unauthenticated and fetch arbitrary MT objects by id using server credentials, leaking counterparty PII/bank details to anyone who can enumerate ids.
gaps.fix_direction: Require auth and authorize that the requested object belongs to the calling merchant/session; ideally remove these debug-style pass-throughs from the public router entirely.

gaps.title: No CORS, rate limiting, or body-size limits on a money API
gaps.detail: The router applies no CorsLayer, no rate/concurrency limiter, and no RequestBodyLimit. Bound to 0.0.0.0, the API is exposed network-wide with unlimited request rates (brute-force of session UUIDs, MT object ids, forged webhooks) and unbounded bodies.
gaps.fix_direction: Add an explicit, restrictive CorsLayer (allowlist admin origin), a tower rate limiter (e.g. tower-governor) especially on initiate/webhook/auth routes, and DefaultBodyLimit; bind to localhost behind a reverse proxy in non-prod.

gaps.title: Non-constant-time webhook signature comparison (Column)
gaps.detail: Column signature check uses `if signature != expected` on hex strings, which is timing-variable and could leak the valid HMAC byte-by-byte; also WEBHOOK_SECRET (.env) is a 32-hex low-entropy value.
gaps.fix_direction: Use a constant-time comparison on the decoded bytes (e.g. Mac::verify_slice or subtle::ConstantTimeEq); rotate WEBHOOK_SECRET to a high-entropy random value and per-provider secrets.

gaps.title: Missing amount/input validation enables negative or out-of-range money values
gaps.detail: amount_cents / amount (i64) are never validated as positive or bounded before creating sessions and transfers, despite AppError::InvalidAmount existing (error.rs:6). merchant_api list_payments also does not clamp limit and computes offset=page*limit unbounded (merchant_api.rs:52-53).
gaps.fix_direction: Validate amounts (>0, sane max, currency) at the boundary; clamp/limit pagination uniformly; reject malformed input with 400 instead of unwrap/panic paths.

gaps.title: Upstream provider error strings leaked to clients
gaps.detail: ColumnError/ModernTreasuryError/PlaidError/AuthError/TemplateError return the raw inner string in the JSON body, potentially exposing provider/internal details to callers (Database/Internal are correctly masked).
gaps.fix_direction: Map provider errors to generic client-facing messages while logging full detail server-side.

gaps.title: Real-looking provider secrets present in on-disk .env loaded at runtime
gaps.detail: .env is gitignored and untracked (good), but contains real-format Modern Treasury, Column, Plaid, DB, and webhook secrets in plaintext on the dev host. Secrets are read ad hoc via std::env::var at call sites (moderntreasury.rs:14, column.rs:12) with no startup validation.
gaps.fix_direction: Source secrets from a secrets manager / injected env in prod; rotate any keys that have lived in shared dev environments; validate required secrets at startup and fail fast; ensure these values are not the same as any production credentials.

gaps.title: admin_handler builds filesystem path from URL (path-traversal smell)
gaps.detail: admin_handler derives admin/dist/{clean} from the request path via strip_prefix and [1..] slicing without canonicalization/containment checks. axum normalizes most traversal, but the construction is fragile for a static-file server.
gaps.fix_direction: Serve the SPA via tower_http ServeDir/ServeFile (which enforces containment) instead of hand-rolled fs reads, or canonicalize and verify the resolved path stays within admin/dist.

risks: READ-ONLY audit: no files were modified. Findings are based on source reading; runtime behavior (e.g. whether a reverse proxy adds auth in deployment) was not observed and could change exposure.
The .env secrets appear real-format; if they are live provider credentials they should be treated as compromised given they were readable in this environment and should be rotated.
Did not exhaustively read every admin SPA / web page; auth assessment of the frontend is based on api.ts and grep, which show no token/login flow — consistent with the unauthenticated backend.
Modern Treasury webhook signature scheme was not cross-checked against MT docs; the finding is that NO verification exists, regardless of scheme.

audits.summary:
Definitive finding: double-entry postings are NEVER written anywhere in the payment flow, and balances are not computed at all — they are hardcoded to zero.

LEDGER WRITE PATH (does not exist): crates/paybank-db/src/ledger_repo.rs defines a complete-looking LedgerRepo with create_journal_entry (ledger_repo.rs:8), create_posting (ledger_repo.rs:28), verify_balance (ledger_repo.rs:52), and get_account (ledger_repo.rs:83). The SQL these run against is correct against the schema (journal_entries / ledger_postings / ledger_accounts in migrations/001_initial_schema.sql:106-139). BUT a full-codebase grep shows LedgerRepo and all four methods have ZERO call sites. The struct is exported via crates/paybank-db/src/lib.rs:5 and then never used. No code path inserts into journal_entries or ledger_postings. So although create_journal_entry hardcodes status='posted', nothing ever calls it.

PAYMENT/SETTLEMENT FLOW (writes transactions only, no ledger): Money-movement settlement happens in two places — crates/paybank-api/src/routes/initiate.rs:74 and crates/paybank-api/src/routes/webhooks.rs:122 — both of which call paybank_db::transaction_repo::create_transaction. That function (crates/paybank-db/src/transaction_repo.rs:7-26) does a single INSERT into the flat `transactions` table and nothing else. It does not open a sqlx transaction, does not create a journal entry, and does not create debit/credit postings. Notably webhooks.rs:122 discards the result with `let _ =`, so even transaction-row failures are swallowed during settlement. The ledger tables are therefore permanently empty in production except for the 4 seed accounts.

BALANCE READ PATH (hardcoded): The only balance endpoint is get_balance in crates/paybank-api/src/routes/merchant_api.rs:21-31, routed at crates/paybank-api/src/router.rs:88 (GET /api/merchant-api/balances/:merchant_id). It ignores AppState entirely (State(_state)), queries nothing, and returns available: 0, pending: 0, currency "USD". So balances are not derived from the ledger, not derived from the transactions table, and not derived from anything — they are constant zero. verify_balance, which would enforce the debits==credits invariant, is likewise never invoked, so the double-entry balancing constraint is never checked.

SCHEMA THAT EXISTS BUT IS UNUSED: migrations/001_initial_schema.sql:106-139 defines ledger_accounts (id, name, type, merchant_id, currency), journal_entries (id, session_id, description, status), and ledger_postings (journal_entry_id, account_id, amount_cents, direction). migrations/002_seed_data.sql:40-44 seeds exactly four accounts for the single demo merchant 00000000-...-0001: Cash (asset), Receivables (asset), Revenue (revenue), Settlement (liability). No other merchant gets ledger accounts, and get_account looks accounts up by (name, merchant_id), so even if wiring were added it would only resolve for the demo merchant.

WHAT CORRECT WIRING WOULD REQUIRE (given existing schema): (1) In the settlement path (webhooks.rs ~122 and initiate.rs ~74), replace the bare create_transaction call with a single sqlx Transaction that: begins a tx; inserts the transactions row; calls LedgerRepo::create_journal_entry(tx, Some(session_id), description); resolves the relevant LedgerRepo::get_account rows for that merchant (e.g. debit Cash/Receivables, credit Settlement/Revenue) — note get_account currently takes a non-null merchant_id and Copy executor, but ledger_accounts.merchant_id is nullable, so platform/house accounts would need a variant; calls create_posting twice (one debit, one credit, equal amounts); calls verify_balance and aborts/rolls back the whole tx if it returns false; commits atomically so the transactions row and its postings are all-or-nothing. (2) Per-merchant ledger accounts must be provisioned at merchant onboarding, since only the demo merchant is seeded. (3) get_balance must be rewritten to compute a balance by summing ledger_postings joined to ledger_accounts for the merchant (SUM of credits minus debits, sign depending on account type), distinguishing posted vs pending journal_entries.status to populate available vs pending — instead of returning hardcoded zeros. (4) Money-safety hardening: a CHECK or trigger enforcing per-journal-entry debit==credit at the DB level, an amount_cents > 0 / direction IN ('debit','credit') constraint, and not discarding settlement insert results with `let _ =`.

gaps.title: Double-entry ledger postings are never written in any payment flow
gaps.detail: LedgerRepo::create_journal_entry / create_posting / verify_balance have no call sites anywhere in the codebase (grep across crates/ and src/ returns only the definition and lib.rs:5 re-export). Settlement at webhooks.rs:122 and initiate.rs:74 only inserts a flat row into the transactions table via transaction_repo::create_transaction (transaction_repo.rs:7), which performs no journal entry and no debit/credit postings. The journal_entries and ledger_postings tables stay permanently empty (apart from no seed). For a regulated money-movement product this means there is no double-entry record of any money movement at all.
gaps.fix_direction: Wire the settlement path to open one sqlx Transaction that inserts the transaction row AND calls create_journal_entry + two balanced create_postings (debit one account, credit another for equal amount_cents) + verify_balance, committing atomically and rolling back if unbalanced.

gaps.title: Balance endpoint returns hardcoded 0/0 — balances are never computed
gaps.detail: get_balance ignores AppState (State(_state)), runs no query, and unconditionally returns available: 0, pending: 0. There is no aggregation over ledger_postings, transactions, or anything else. Any merchant-facing or admin balance display is therefore a constant lie regardless of actual settled funds.
gaps.fix_direction: Compute balance by summing ledger_postings (credits minus debits) joined to ledger_accounts for the merchant once postings exist; split available vs pending by journal_entries.status (posted vs pending). Until the ledger is wired, at minimum derive from settled transactions rather than returning a constant.

gaps.title: verify_balance invariant (debits==credits) is never enforced
gaps.detail: verify_balance checks debits==credits && debits>0 for a journal entry, but is never called, and there is no DB-level CHECK/trigger enforcing balanced entries, valid direction values, or positive amounts. So nothing — neither application code nor schema — guarantees the core double-entry invariant. ledger_postings.direction and amount_cents are unconstrained TEXT/BIGINT (migrations/001_initial_schema.sql:129-136).
gaps.fix_direction: Call verify_balance inside the posting transaction and abort on false; additionally add DB constraints: direction IN ('debit','credit'), amount_cents > 0, and ideally a deferred trigger asserting SUM(debit)=SUM(credit) per journal_entry_id.

gaps.title: Ledger accounts only exist for the single demo merchant
gaps.detail: Only merchant 00000000-...-0001 gets the 4 ledger accounts (Cash/Receivables/Revenue/Settlement). No onboarding code provisions ledger_accounts for new merchants, and get_account (ledger_repo.rs:83) looks up by (name, merchant_id), so even if posting were wired it would fetch_one-error for every real merchant. Also ledger_accounts.merchant_id is nullable (for platform/house accounts) but get_account's signature requires a non-null Uuid.
gaps.fix_direction: Provision the standard chart of accounts per merchant at onboarding; add a get_account variant (or merchant_id Option) to resolve platform-level accounts with NULL merchant_id.

gaps.title: Settlement transaction insert result is discarded, hiding failures
gaps.detail: create_transaction is called as `let _ = ...`, so a failed insert during webhook-driven settlement is silently ignored — the session may be marked Completed while no transactions row (and, once added, no ledger entry) was persisted. This is a money-safety reconciliation gap.
gaps.fix_direction: Propagate/handle the error, and once ledger wiring exists make the transaction-row + journal-entry insert a single atomic DB transaction whose failure prevents marking the session completed.

risks: Conclusions are based on static reading and full-codebase grep for the ledger symbols and SQL table names; I did not run the app or inspect a live DB, but the absence of call sites is definitive from source.
I focused on the ledger/balance subsystem; admin-side balance/reporting screens in admin/ may also consume the hardcoded-zero endpoint but were not individually audited.
PaymentRail::choose and provider settlement semantics were not deeply audited beyond confirming they terminate in create_transaction.

audits.subsystem: Webhooks (inbound provider callbacks + outbound merchant notifications)
audits.summary:
There are exactly two inbound webhook endpoints, wired in crates/paybank-api/src/router.rs:86-87: POST /api/webhooks/column -> column_webhook and POST /api/webhooks/moderntreasury -> moderntreasury_webhook (both in crates/paybank-api/src/routes/webhooks.rs). There is NO outbound merchant-webhook system in operation.

INBOUND - Column (webhooks.rs:17-87): It does verify a signature. It loads WEBHOOK_SECRET from env, computes HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body bytes, hex-encodes it, and compares against the `column-signature` header (lines 22-41). It then parses `data.id`/`data.status`, extracts a session id from `data.description` by stripping the literal prefix "Session " and parsing a UUID (lines 49-53), and drives session transitions via session_repo::update_status: settled/completed -> Completed, failed/returned -> Expired, anything else -> Processing (lines 54-83). So inbound Column events DO transition session status. Caveats: (a) the comparison `signature != expected` (line 35) is a non-constant-time string compare (timing side-channel on signature verification); (b) the secret is a single shared global WEBHOOK_SECRET, not per-merchant/per-provider; (c) the HMAC scheme assumed (raw-body hex HMAC, no timestamp/version) does not match Column's documented signing scheme, so this verification is unlikely to actually validate real Column signatures.

INBOUND - Modern Treasury (webhooks.rs:89-137): This is the PRIMARY provider, yet the handler takes only State + Bytes and NEVER verifies any signature - no HeaderMap parameter, no X-Signature/X-Timestamp check at all. It is a completely unauthenticated, publicly reachable endpoint that mutates payment-session state. It parses event_type/resource.id/resource.status, extracts session id from resource.remittance_information ("Session <uuid>"), and maps status settled/completed -> Completed, failed/returned/reversed -> Expired, else event_type==payment_order.settled -> Completed, else None (lines 108-118). So MT events do drive transitions, but the endpoint can be forged by anyone to mark sessions Completed/Expired.

STATUS-MODEL DEFECT: SessionStatus (crates/paybank-core/src/models.rs:103-109) only has Pending, Authorized, Processing, Completed, Expired. There is NO Returned or Reversed variant. Both handlers therefore collapse returned/reversed/failed into Expired. In a money-movement product this is wrong and dangerous: a payment that was Completed and then returned/reversed by the network gets marked Expired, conflating "never funded / timed out" with "funds clawed back," and losing the distinction needed for reconciliation, refunds, and merchant notification. (PaymentStatus at models.rs does have Returned/Reversed, but session status, which the webhooks write, does not.)

BOGUS TRANSACTION WRITE: The MT handler (webhooks.rs:120-134) inserts a transaction with amount 0, counterparty Uuid::nil(), and rail hardcoded to FedNow on every webhook with a non-empty transfer id, regardless of the real rail or amount. The result is ignored (`let _ =`), so failures are silently swallowed, and the data written is fabricated.

OUTBOUND merchant webhooks: NON-FUNCTIONAL. The schema is fully built out - webhook_events (migrations/001_initial_schema.sql:156-167) with status/attempts/next_retry_at/sent_at, plus webhook_delivery_logs (lines 176-187) and queue indexes idx_webhook_events_queue/idx_webhook_events_pending (lines 172-173) explicitly designed for a retry worker. Merchants have webhook_url and webhook_secret columns (lines 7-8). The WebhookEvent/WebhookDelivery models exist (models.rs:398-423). BUT: there is no INSERT into webhook_events anywhere in the codebase (grep across crates/ and src/ finds only a single read path, admin_repo::list_webhook_events at crates/paybank-db/src/admin_repo.rs:275-291, surfaced read-only via GET /api/admin/webhooks). No code ever enqueues an outbound event, and no background delivery worker exists - src/main.rs (1-32) only runs migrations and starts axum; there is no tokio::spawn, no loop, nothing polling next_retry_at. The only reqwest::Client usages are outbound calls to Column/MT/Plaid provider APIs, not merchant delivery. Net effect: when a provider webhook updates a session to Completed/Expired, the merchant is NEVER notified. The entire outbound webhook subsystem (tables, retry columns, indexes, models, admin list view) is dead scaffolding.

gaps.title: Modern Treasury webhook has NO signature verification (primary provider, unauthenticated state mutation)
gaps.detail: moderntreasury_webhook takes only State and Bytes - no HeaderMap, no signature/timestamp check. The endpoint POST /api/webhooks/moderntreasury (router.rs:87) is publicly reachable and directly calls session_repo::update_status to set sessions to Completed or Expired (lines 108-118). Any attacker who knows or guesses a session UUID can forge a request to mark a payment Completed (falsely releasing goods/funds) or Expired. MT is the primary money-movement provider, so this is a critical authenticity hole.
gaps.fix_direction: Add HeaderMap, read MT's signature header, recompute HMAC over the raw body using the configured MT webhook signing secret, and reject on mismatch using a constant-time comparison BEFORE any parsing or DB mutation. Match Modern Treasury's documented signing scheme exactly.

gaps.title: Outbound merchant webhook system is entirely non-functional (no enqueue, no delivery worker)
gaps.detail: webhook_events / webhook_delivery_logs tables, attempts/next_retry_at retry columns, and queue indexes all exist (migrations/001_initial_schema.sql:156-189), but nothing ever INSERTs a webhook_events row (grep finds only the read path admin_repo::list_webhook_events:275-291) and no background delivery worker exists (main.rs has no tokio::spawn / polling loop). When inbound provider webhooks transition a session to Completed/Expired, the merchant is never notified. Merchants integrating against Depost will never receive payment.completed / payment.failed callbacks - a core promised platform feature is missing.
gaps.fix_direction: On each session status transition (in both webhook handlers and any other status-changing path), INSERT a webhook_events row (merchant_id, session_id, event_type, payload, status='pending'). Add a background worker spawned from main.rs that polls webhook_events where status in pending/failed and next_retry_at <= now, POSTs to merchant.webhook_url with an HMAC signature using merchant.webhook_secret, records attempts in webhook_delivery_logs, and applies exponential backoff via next_retry_at with a max-attempts cap.

gaps.title: SessionStatus lacks Returned/Reversed - returns and reversals silently mapped to Expired
gaps.detail: SessionStatus only has Pending/Authorized/Processing/Completed/Expired. Both handlers map provider 'returned'/'reversed'/'failed' to SessionStatus::Expired. A previously-Completed payment that the network later returns or reverses (clawback) becomes 'Expired', conflating funds-clawed-back with never-funded/timed-out. This destroys reconciliation accuracy and means merchants cannot distinguish a real return from an expiry - a money-safety correctness defect in a regulated product. Note PaymentStatus (models.rs) does define Returned/Reversed, but session status does not.
gaps.fix_direction: Add Returned and Reversed variants to SessionStatus (and the corresponding allowed values in the payment_sessions.status column), map provider returned->Returned and reversed->Reversed distinctly, and ensure ledger reversal/refund logic and merchant webhooks fire on those transitions.

gaps.title: Fabricated zero-amount FedNow transaction inserted on every MT webhook, errors swallowed
gaps.detail: On any MT webhook with a non-empty transfer_id, the handler inserts a transaction_repo row with amount 0, counterparty Uuid::nil(), and rail hardcoded to PaymentRail::FedNow regardless of the actual rail or amount, and discards the result with `let _ =` so any DB error is silently ignored. This writes false financial records (wrong/zero amount, nil counterparty, wrong rail) and hides failures.
gaps.fix_direction: Either remove this speculative insert or populate it from the actual resource fields (real amount, rail, counterparty) only for the specific settlement event types, propagate errors instead of discarding, and guard against duplicate inserts on webhook retries (idempotency on transfer_id).

gaps.title: Non-constant-time signature comparison in Column handler
gaps.detail: `if signature != expected` compares the HMAC digest with a standard string equality, which short-circuits and is vulnerable to timing analysis on the webhook signature.
gaps.fix_direction: Compare using a constant-time equality (e.g. feed expected bytes into Mac::verify_slice, or use a constant-time-eq comparator) rather than `!=`.

gaps.title: Column signature scheme likely incorrect and uses a single shared global secret
gaps.detail: Verification assumes raw-body-HMAC-hex with a single env WEBHOOK_SECRET. Column's real signing scheme typically involves a versioned/timestamped signing string, so this check probably will not validate genuine Column signatures (and shares one secret across providers/merchants). On any signing-secret misconfiguration the handler returns Internal errors (missing secret/header treated as 500 via AppError::Internal at lines 23/28) rather than a clean 401/400.
gaps.fix_direction: Implement Column's documented signature construction (including any timestamp/version prefix and replay window), use the Column-specific secret, and return 401 for auth failures rather than 500.

risks: Both inbound handlers always return 200 with {received:true} on the happy path; the MT handler returns None for unknown statuses without surfacing/logging unhandled event types, so silent no-ops are possible if remittance_information formatting differs.

Session lookup depends on the provider echoing back a 'Session <uuid>' string in description (Column) / remittance_information (MT). If the provider truncates or omits this field, the webhook silently fails to update any session with no alerting.
WEBHOOK_SECRET being absent causes a 500 (AppError::Internal) on every Column webhook, which could mask a misconfiguration as a transient provider error.
No idempotency/dedup on inbound webhooks: providers retry deliveries, and update_status plus the transaction insert will run repeatedly, compounding the fabricated-transaction issue.

audits.summary:
The schema is defined entirely in two files run via `sqlx::migrate!("./migrations")` at startup (src/main.rs:20): 001_initial_schema.sql (DDL) and 002_seed_data.sql (seed). No versioning beyond filename ordering and no down migrations.

Tables (11): merchants, banks, payment_sessions, transactions, payment_attempts, ledger_accounts, journal_entries, ledger_postings, idempotency_keys, webhook_events, webhook_delivery_logs.

Money is stored consistently as cents in BIGINT (amount_cents) across payment_sessions, transactions, ledger_postings — correct vs float, and NOT NULL where it matters.

PII: payment_sessions stores the customer's full bank account number and routing number in plaintext TEXT (001:60-61). Written by update_customer_details (session_repo.rs:129-164), read back by get_session/list_sessions (session_repo.rs:36-127), used to build the Column transfer in confirm.rs:46-54, and surfaced to the admin UI via admin_repo::list_all_sessions (admin_repo.rs:128-140) → admin/src/lib/api.ts:32-33 / Sessions.tsx:121. No encryption, tokenization, masking, or column-level access control.

Idempotency: idempotency_keys is well-designed (composite PK (merchant_id, idempotency_key), expires_at, state, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING in idempotency_repo.rs:11-52) but COMPLETELY UNUSED — no references to try_acquire_key/complete_key/IdempotencyRepo in crates/paybank-api or src. CreatePaymentRequest.idempotency_key (models.rs:268) is accepted but never enforced, so duplicate payment creation is not prevented.

Model/schema drift: models.rs defines a Payment struct (213-248) with columns (idempotency_key, method, provider_reference, metadata, authorization_url, session_status, etc.) that have NO backing table — there is no `payments` table in either migration and no query references one. The real table is payment_sessions ↔ PaymentSession (320-346). Payment is dead/aspirational.
