Indexes: good coverage on merchants, transactions, payment_attempts, webhook_events (incl. partial retry-queue indexes). Gaps on the hottest admin list path (status+created_at ordering, rail_used).

Seed hardcodes two demo merchants with fixed UUIDs (00000000-...-0001/0002) and guessable plaintext API keys 'pb_test_1234567890abcdef' / 'pb_test_abcdef1234567890' (002:5-25), status active / kyc verified, plus four ledger accounts only for merchant 0001 (002:40-45). 002 runs unconditionally on every env via sqlx::migrate! with no prod guard; merchant 0002 and new merchants get no ledger accounts.

gaps.title: Customer bank account number and routing number stored in plaintext
gaps.detail: payment_sessions.customer_account_number and customer_routing_number are plain TEXT, written via update_customer_details (session_repo.rs:154-155) and read back unmasked by get_session, list_sessions, and admin_repo::list_all_sessions, then returned to the admin SPA (admin/src/lib/api.ts:32-33, Sessions.tsx:121). Full DDA + routing is effectively a payment credential; cleartext storage exposes it via DB dumps, backups, logs, and any admin-token compromise.
gaps.fix_direction: Encrypt at rest (app-level envelope/KMS or pgcrypto) or tokenize via the provider; store only last-4 + token. Never select full account into list endpoints; mask in API responses and restrict read access.

gaps.title: idempotency_keys table exists but is never used; no duplicate-payment protection
gaps.detail: The acquire/complete repo is fully implemented but has zero callers (no try_acquire_key/complete_key/IdempotencyRepo references in crates/paybank-api or src). CreatePaymentRequest.idempotency_key (models.rs:268) is accepted but never enforced, so a retried create request creates a second money-moving session/transfer with no dedupe.
gaps.fix_direction: Wire IdempotencyRepo into the create handler within a DB transaction: acquire on entry, short-circuit returning the stored response on conflict-with-completed, complete_key before commit. Require the header for mutating money endpoints.

gaps.title: Payment model has no backing table - schema/model drift
gaps.detail: The Payment struct describes a `payments` table (idempotency_key, method, provider_reference, metadata, authorization_url, session_status, etc.) that exists in no migration and is queried nowhere; real persistence is payment_sessions/PaymentSession. The dead model invites queries against a nonexistent table and obscures the true data model.
gaps.fix_direction: Remove Payment, or actually introduce a payments table and migrate logic onto it. Reconcile every FromRow struct in models.rs with the migrations.

gaps.title: Missing composite index for the admin sessions list hot path
gaps.detail: list_all_sessions filters payment_sessions by status/rail_used/date then ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT/OFFSET plus COUNT(*). Only single-column idx_payment_sessions_merchant and idx_payment_sessions_status exist (001:69-70). No index backs (status, created_at) ordering or rail_used, so admin list and dashboard queries (status filters + created_at, GROUP BY rail_used) seq-scan and sort, degrading as the table grows.
gaps.fix_direction: Add (status, created_at DESC), an index on rail_used or (rail_used, created_at), and (merchant_id, created_at DESC) for the merchant-scoped list. Prefer keyset pagination over OFFSET.

gaps.title: No CHECK constraints on enum-like status/type columns or money sign
gaps.detail: status, kyc_status, risk_level, payment_sessions.status, ledger_accounts.type, ledger_postings.direction, idempotency_keys.state, webhook_events.status are free-form TEXT with no CHECK/enum, so any value can be written and silently break Rust enum decode (the Rust SessionStatus/PaymentStatus enums use distinct string sets). amount_cents columns lack CHECK (>0) and ledger_postings.direction is unconstrained, so negative/unbalanced postings are accepted by the DB.
gaps.fix_direction: Add CHECK constraints or Postgres ENUMs matching the Rust enums for each status/type/direction column, CHECK (amount_cents > 0) where appropriate, and enforce double-entry balance via constraint/trigger.

gaps.title: Predictable plaintext demo API keys and fixed merchant UUIDs in seed; runs in every env
gaps.detail: Seed inserts demo merchants with well-known UUIDs (00000000-...-0001/0002) and guessable cleartext API keys (pb_test_1234567890abcdef, pb_test_abcdef1234567890), status active, kyc verified. The migration runs unconditionally via sqlx::migrate! (main.rs:20); if shipped to prod these are live credentials granting authenticated API access.
gaps.fix_direction: Move seed out of the migration set or gate it on an env flag. Never ship active verified merchants with static keys; store only hashed api_key and generate per-environment.

gaps.title: API keys and webhook secrets stored in plaintext
gaps.detail: merchants.api_key and webhook_secret are plain TEXT (api_key UNIQUE). Auth compares the raw key, so a single DB read discloses every merchant's live API credential and webhook signing secret.
gaps.fix_direction: Store a hash of the API key (HMAC/argon2 with a lookup prefix) and encrypt webhook_secret at rest; compare hashes on auth.

gaps.title: Seed creates ledger accounts only for merchant 0001; double-entry fails for others
gaps.detail: Only merchant 0001 gets Cash/Receivables/Revenue/Settlement accounts. Merchant 0002 and newly registered merchants have none, so ledger flows keyed on these account roles fail or silently skip. ledger_accounts.merchant_id is nullable with no uniqueness on (merchant_id, type), allowing duplicate/ambiguous roles.
gaps.fix_direction: Provision a standard chart of accounts on merchant creation, and add UNIQUE (merchant_id, type).

gaps.title: Missing FK indexes, NOT NULL gaps, and nullable provider vs non-Option Rust field
gaps.detail: payment_sessions.bank_id is an unindexed FK (only merchant_id is indexed); webhook_delivery_logs has no created_at index; transactions has no index on settled_at/created_at used in settlement reporting. provider is VARCHAR(50) NULL with no default while Rust Payment.provider is a non-Option String (models.rs:225) and Transaction has no provider field at all despite the column existing — a decode mismatch risk for NULL rows. ledger_accounts.merchant_id is a nullable FK.
gaps.fix_direction: Add indexes on payment_sessions(bank_id), webhook_delivery_logs(created_at), and reporting date columns; reconcile the nullable provider column with the Rust field type (NOT NULL DEFAULT or Option<String>).

audits.subsystem: Admin & Merchant APIs + frontend wiring (crates/paybank-api/src/routes/{admin,merchant_api}.rs, admin/src, web/dashboard.html)
audits.summary:
Two distinct API surfaces feed two distinct UIs.

ADMIN API (/api/admin/*, routes/admin.rs -> paybank-db/admin_repo.rs) backs the redesigned React console in admin/src. Endpoints: stats, sessions (list+detail), merchants (list/get/create/update), banks, settlements, webhooks. All return serde_json::Value envelopes built by hand. The React client (admin/src/lib/api.ts) declares matching TS interfaces and the pages consume them. Response shapes mostly line up: stats -> DashboardStats (today_total_transactions/today_completed/pending_count/total_volume_cents/by_rail[{rail_used,count,volume}]/last_7_days[{date,count,volume}]) matches admin_repo::DashboardStats exactly; list_sessions returns {sessions,total} consumed by Sessions.tsx/Dashboard.tsx; list_merchants {merchants,total}; banks {banks}; settlements {settlements} (SettlementRow fields merchant_id/merchant_name/total_count/total_volume_cents/last_payment_date all match); webhooks {events,total}. Pagination is server-clamped (limit default 50, .min(200), offset default 0) and the session filter supports status/rail/date_from/date_to via dynamically-built parameterized SQL (admin_repo.rs:82-168) — bind order is correct and values are parameterized (no SQL injection; column names are not user-controlled). Sorting is created_at DESC. The frontend mostly fetches with limit=100/200 and does NOT send offset, so there is effectively no pagination UI — large datasets silently truncate at the limit and totals are shown only as nav counts.

MERCHANT API (/api/merchant-api/*, routes/merchant_api.rs) backs the legacy customer/merchant page web/dashboard.html. This surface is largely stubbed: get_balance ignores the DB entirely and always returns available:0/pending:0/USD (merchant_api.rs:21-31); get_merchant_profile returns hardcoded active/verified JSON (merchant_api.rs:33-39); payment_timeseries returns [] (merchant_api.rs:80-82); list_payments hardcodes DEMO_MERCHANT_ID = 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001 (merchant_api.rs:11,51), ignoring any auth/merchant context, hardcodes status:"settled", currency:"USD", provider:"moderntreasury" for every row regardless of actual state, discards the real total, and returns {payments:[...]} with no pagination total. create_payment_link also hardcodes DEMO_MERCHANT_ID and a single hardcoded routing number 021000021 (merchant_api.rs:104-105). dashboard.html hardcodes the same MERCHANT_ID (web/dashboard.html:181) and tolerates the balance stub via .catch fallback (line 249).

NEITHER surface has any authentication/authorization — every /api/admin/* and /api/merchant-api/* route in router.rs:88-106 is unauthenticated. Anyone who can reach the server can list all merchants (including secrets), all sessions with full customer bank account/routing numbers, create merchants, and edit merchant tax_id/webhook_url.

gaps.title: Admin merchant endpoints leak password_hash and api_key to the client
gaps.detail: list_merchants/get_merchant/create_merchant/update_merchant all SELECT password_hash and api_key and return the full paybank_core::Merchant struct, which is serialized with default serde and has no #[serde(skip)] on password_hash (models.rs:155). The admin handlers (admin.rs:89-136) serialize the whole struct to JSON. So GET /api/admin/merchants returns every merchant's bcrypt/argon password_hash and live api_key over the wire. A dedicated MerchantResponse exists (models.rs:198-211) that omits password_hash but is NOT used here. The TS Merchant interface (api.ts:40-58) even declares api_key:string, confirming the secret reaches the browser. In a regulated money product this is a credential-exfiltration vector.
gaps.fix_direction: Return MerchantResponse (or a redacted DTO) from admin handlers instead of the raw Merchant; never select/serialize password_hash; treat api_key as a secret (mask or omit). Add #[serde(skip_serializing)] to Merchant.password_hash as defense-in-depth.

gaps.title: All admin and merchant API endpoints are completely unauthenticated
gaps.detail: No auth middleware/layer is applied to /api/admin/* or /api/merchant-api/*. There is no API-key check, no session/cookie auth, no merchant scoping. Any unauthenticated caller can enumerate all merchants (with secrets, see above), list every payment session including full customer PII and raw bank account_number/routing_number (admin_repo.rs:129-137 selects customer_account_number/customer_routing_number and admin.rs:53-71 returns them), create merchants, and mutate merchant tax_id/webhook_url (a webhook_url rewrite enables redirecting future webhook deliveries). The admin SPA itself ships unauthenticated via the admin_handler static server (router.rs:30-69).
gaps.fix_direction: Add an auth layer (admin bearer/session for /api/admin/*; per-merchant API key for /api/merchant-api/*) and scope merchant-api queries to the authenticated merchant rather than DEMO_MERCHANT_ID. Strip raw bank numbers from admin session payloads unless the operator role explicitly warrants it.

gaps.title: Merchant-api balance/profile/timeseries are inert stubs returning fabricated data
gaps.detail: get_balance always returns available:0/pending:0 ignoring the ledger entirely; get_merchant_profile returns a hardcoded {status:active,kyc_status:verified} regardless of the real merchant; payment_timeseries returns []. dashboard.html:249-253 renders the fake zero balance, and the chart/profile areas show fabricated 'verified' status. For a money product, surfacing a hardcoded 'verified' KYC and a fake $0 balance is misleading and unsafe. There is a real ledger_repo in paybank-db that is not consulted.
gaps.fix_direction: Wire get_balance to ledger_repo for the authenticated merchant, source profile from merchants table, and implement timeseries from payment_sessions/transactions; or remove the endpoints and their UI until backed by real data.

gaps.title: list_payments hardcodes DEMO_MERCHANT_ID and fakes per-row status/currency/provider
gaps.detail: Every request returns transactions for the single demo merchant regardless of who calls. Each payment row is emitted with status:"settled", currency:"USD", provider:"moderntreasury" hardcoded (lines 63-66) even though the underlying Transaction has no status field and rail_used may differ; a transaction that failed/returned would still display as settled. The real total from list_transactions is discarded (let (_, _total)) and the {payments} envelope has no total, so the dashboard cannot paginate.
gaps.fix_direction: Scope to the authenticated merchant; derive status from the session/payment record rather than hardcoding 'settled'; include total in the response; do not assume USD/moderntreasury per row.

gaps.title: Webhook Retry and View buttons are inert; no retry endpoint exists
gaps.location: admin/src/pages/Webhooks.tsx:42-51; router.rs (no route); whole crates/paybank-api/src (grep for retry/resend = none)
gaps.detail: The Webhooks page renders a 'Retry' button for failed events and a 'View' button for others, but neither has an onClick handler and api.ts exposes no retry/resend/get-detail method. There is no /api/admin/webhooks/:id/retry (or any retry) route in router.rs and no retry handler anywhere in the API. The UI promises webhook redelivery (App.tsx:28 nav subtitle 'Event delivery log and retries') that the backend cannot perform. webhook_events.next_retry_at/attempts are read-only here.
gaps.fix_direction: Implement a POST /api/admin/webhooks/:id/retry that re-enqueues delivery and updates attempts/next_retry_at, wire api.ts + the button onClick, and add an event-detail view; until then the buttons should be removed to avoid implying functionality.

gaps.title: Admin SPA fetches with limit only and no offset; no real pagination despite total being returned
gaps.location: admin/src/pages/Sessions.tsx:18, Merchants.tsx:8, Webhooks.tsx:7, Settlements.tsx (no limit), App.tsx:38-43
gaps.detail: All list pages request a fixed limit (100/200) and never pass offset, so beyond that cap rows are silently dropped even though the backend returns total and supports offset. Sessions.tsx and Merchants.tsx ignore the returned total entirely (only App.tsx uses sessions total/merchants length as nav badges). For an operations console on a money product, silently truncating the session/merchant ledger at 100-200 rows is an integrity risk for reconciliation.
gaps.fix_direction: Add offset-based or cursor pagination controls in the UI and surface total; or at minimum display a 'showing N of total' indicator and a load-more.

gaps.title: create_payment_link hardcodes a single routing number and demo merchant
gaps.detail: Payment links are always created under DEMO_MERCHANT_ID and always against bank 021000021, ignoring the merchant context and the request's country/method fields (req.country/req.method are parsed but unused; only amount/description feed the session). The rail is chosen from that one hardcoded bank's capabilities, so the rail selection is unrelated to the actual paying bank. This produces sessions attributed to the wrong merchant in a real deployment.
gaps.fix_direction: Derive merchant from auth, select bank from request/customer context, and honor or remove the unused country/method fields.

gaps.title: Unwrap on serde_json::to_value in admin handlers can panic on serialization edge cases
gaps.detail: Handlers call serde_json::to_value(...).unwrap(). These structs serialize cleanly today, so this is low risk, but a panic in a request handler aborts the task and returns a 500 with no structured error; in a money-movement service handler panics should be avoided. get_session_detail (admin.rs:73-81) and get_merchant (admin.rs:95-103) also serialize an Option to JSON null on not-found and return 200 rather than 404.
gaps.fix_direction: Map serialization errors to AppError instead of unwrap; return 404 when get_session/get_merchant yield None.

audits.summary:
Boot/runtime (src/main.rs): main() loads .env via dotenvy, initializes tracing with bare `tracing_subscriber::fmt::init()` (no JSON, no EnvFilter wired even though the `json`/`env-filter` features are enabled in Cargo.toml lines 25), reads DATABASE_URL (panics via .expect if missing), builds a Postgres pool with ONLY `.max_connections(10)` (no min_connections, acquire_timeout, idle_timeout, or max_lifetime), runs `sqlx::migrate!("./migrations")` on every boot (migrations are embedded at compile time so the source dir need not ship), then `axum::serve(listener, router).await` with NO graceful-shutdown signal handler. BIND_ADDR defaults to 0.0.0.0:3000 but Docker/compose use 8888.

Router (crates/paybank-api/src/router.rs): build_router wires routes and a `/health` endpoint that is a static `get(|| async { "OK" })` (line 73) — no DB readiness/liveness probe. Despite `tower-http` being pulled in with the `trace` and `cors` features (crates/paybank-api/Cargo.toml line 16), NO middleware is layered onto the router at all: no TraceLayer (so no per-request access logs / latency / status logging), no request-ID propagation, no CorsLayer, no timeout layer, no body-limit layer, no panic-catch layer. There is zero metrics endpoint (no Prometheus/OpenTelemetry) and no error-tracking integration (no Sentry). Observability is effectively just whatever the handlers manually `tracing::info!`.

Config handling: there is no central typed Config struct validated at startup. Provider/runtime config is read lazily via scattered `std::env::var(...)` calls inside request handlers and provider constructors (e.g. paybank-payments/src/lib.rs:19-21,75,91; moderntreasury.rs:12-14; column.rs:12; plaid.rs:15-17; webhooks.rs:22; sessions.rs:41,96,166; initiate.rs:40). Missing/misconfigured secrets therefore surface as per-request failures or panics rather than a fail-fast boot error.

Docker (Dockerfile): 3-stage build (node admin build -> rust:1-slim builder with SQLX_OFFLINE=true -> debian:bookworm-slim runtime) which is good for size, BUT the runtime image runs as ROOT (no `USER` directive), has no `HEALTHCHECK`, and has NO `WORKDIR` in the final stage so CWD is `/`. The binary serves static assets via working-dir-relative paths (`web/pay.html`, `web/invoice.html`, `admin/dist/...`, `ServeDir::new("web")` in router.rs:15,23,39,62,110); assets are COPYed to `/web` and `/admin/dist`, which only resolve correctly because CWD happens to be `/` — a fragile coupling. EXPOSE 8888 matches compose but not the code default 3000.

Secrets: real-looking live API keys/secrets (Column, Modern Treasury, Plaid, WEBHOOK_SECRET) are hardcoded in docker-compose.yml (lines 29-37) and committed in .env-equivalent values; .env itself is gitignored (git check-ignore confirms) and not in git history, but docker-compose.yml IS tracked and carries the same secrets. appsmith/docker-compose.yml is also tracked with hardcoded encryption password/salt (lines 9-10).

CI/CD & repo hygiene: there is NO .github/workflows directory — no CI, no automated build/test/lint/security scan, no CD. Leftover operational cruft is tracked in git: appsmith/ (full Appsmith service compose), and two helper Python scripts drop_all.py (drops the entire public schema) and run_migrations.py (both hardcode the DB password and point at a stale DB name `paybank_monolith` that does not match the current `noralpay` DB, so they are broken/dangerous if run).

gaps.title: Live provider secrets committed to git in docker-compose.yml
gaps.detail: Real-looking Column (COLUMN_API_KEY), Modern Treasury (MODERN_TREASURY_API_KEY) and Plaid (PLAID_SECRET) credentials plus WEBHOOK_SECRET are hardcoded into the tracked docker-compose.yml, and the same values live in .env. For a regulated money-movement product these are money-moving and webhook-auth secrets sitting in source control history. appsmith/docker-compose.yml:9-10 likewise commits encryption password/salt. .env is gitignored but docker-compose.yml is not.
gaps.fix_direction: Rotate all exposed provider keys and the webhook secret immediately. Move secrets out of docker-compose.yml into a secret manager / untracked env file referenced via env_file or compose secrets. Scrub git history if any key was ever real.

gaps.title: No graceful shutdown on axum::serve
gaps.detail: axum::serve(listener, router).await runs with no .with_graceful_shutdown() and no SIGTERM/SIGINT handler. On deploy/rollout the process is hard-killed mid-request, which can interrupt in-flight payment-order creation/confirmation and webhook processing, risking partial/inconsistent money-movement state and dropped DB connections.
gaps.fix_direction: Add a shutdown signal future (tokio::signal ctrl_c + unix SIGTERM) and pass it to axum::serve(...).with_graceful_shutdown(...); ideally drain in-flight requests and close the pool on shutdown.

gaps.title: /health is static, no DB readiness probe
gaps.detail: /health returns a constant "OK" and never checks the database. An instance with a dead/exhausted Postgres pool will report healthy, so orchestrators (k8s, compose has no api healthcheck at all) and load balancers will keep routing payment traffic to a broken instance.
gaps.fix_direction: Add a readiness endpoint that runs a lightweight `SELECT 1` against the pool (with a short timeout) and return 503 on failure; keep a separate cheap liveness endpoint. Wire a Docker HEALTHCHECK / compose healthcheck for the api service.

gaps.title: No request logging / tracing middleware despite enabled features
gaps.detail: tower-http is compiled with the `trace` and `cors` features (crates/paybank-api/Cargo.toml:16) but the router applies no layers at all: no TraceLayer, no request IDs, no CORS, no timeout, no request-body size limit, no panic-recovery. There is therefore no per-request access log, latency, status-code, or correlation-ID observability for a financial API, and unhandled panics in a handler will drop the connection with no captured error.
gaps.fix_direction: Add a layered stack: TraceLayer (make_span with method/path/request-id), a request-id propagation layer (tower-http SetRequestId/PropagateRequestId), a global timeout, RequestBodyLimit, and CatchPanic; configure tracing_subscriber with EnvFilter + JSON in production.

gaps.title: Migrations run on every boot — unsafe for multi-instance / concurrent deploys
gaps.detail: sqlx::migrate!(...).run(&pool) executes on each process start. With multiple API replicas (compose restart:unless-stopped + horizontal scaling) booting concurrently, several instances race to apply migrations. sqlx takes an advisory lock so it is usually safe, but coupling schema migration to app boot still means a bad migration takes the whole fleet down and there is no controlled, auditable migration gate for a regulated DB.
gaps.fix_direction: Move migrations to a dedicated init/job step (separate command or CI/CD migration stage) run once before rollout; keep app boot read-only against schema, or gate auto-migrate behind an env flag used only by the migration job.

gaps.title: No CI/CD pipeline
gaps.detail: There is no .github/workflows directory and no other CI config. For a money-movement codebase there is no automated build, test (tests/ dir is empty), clippy/fmt, cargo-audit/dependency scan, secret scanning, or SQLx offline-cache verification on PRs, and no controlled deploy. Regressions and leaked secrets can ship unchecked.
gaps.fix_direction: Add GitHub Actions: cargo build/test/clippy/fmt, cargo audit + cargo deny, sqlx prepare --check, a secret scanner (gitleaks), and a gated build/push/deploy workflow.

gaps.title: Docker runtime runs as root, no WORKDIR, no HEALTHCHECK
gaps.detail: Final debian:bookworm-slim stage adds no non-root USER (container runs as root), no HEALTHCHECK, and no WORKDIR. The app serves static assets via CWD-relative paths (router.rs:15,23,39,62,110) while assets are copied to /web and /admin/dist; this only works because CWD defaults to /. Any future WORKDIR change or path tweak silently breaks /pay, /invoice, /admin, /static serving.
gaps.fix_direction: Add a non-root user and `USER`, set an explicit WORKDIR matching where assets live (or make asset paths absolute/configurable), and add a HEALTHCHECK hitting the readiness endpoint.

gaps.title: Postgres pool under-configured
gaps.detail: Pool sets only max_connections(10); no acquire_timeout (a saturated pool will hang requests indefinitely instead of failing fast), no idle_timeout/max_lifetime (stale connections behind a proxy/PgBouncer can accumulate), and no min_connections. Under load or a slow DB this causes unbounded request queueing for payment endpoints.
gaps.fix_direction: Set acquire_timeout (e.g. a few seconds), idle_timeout, max_lifetime, and tune max/min_connections for expected concurrency; surface pool errors as 503.

gaps.title: Config read lazily per-request instead of fail-fast at boot
gaps.detail: Provider and app config (MT/Column/Plaid keys, MT_INTERNAL_ACCOUNT_ID, WEBHOOK_SECRET, PUBLIC_APP_URL) is read via scattered std::env::var calls inside handlers/constructors (also moderntreasury.rs:12-14, column.rs:12, plaid.rs:15-17, webhooks.rs:22, sessions.rs:41/96/166, initiate.rs:40). Missing config only fails when the relevant payment path is hit, not at startup, so a misconfigured instance can pass /health and accept traffic before failing a real payment.
gaps.fix_direction: Introduce a single typed Config loaded and validated at startup (fail boot on missing required secrets), store it in AppState, and read from it instead of env at request time.

gaps.title: Default BIND_ADDR mismatches deployment port
gaps.detail: Code defaults BIND_ADDR to 0.0.0.0:3000 while Dockerfile EXPOSE and docker-compose both use 8888. If BIND_ADDR is ever unset in an environment, the app binds 3000 and the container/healthchecks silently fail to reach it.
gaps.fix_direction: Align the default with the deployed port or require BIND_ADDR explicitly; document the single source of truth.

gaps.title: Dangerous/stale helper scripts tracked in repo
gaps.detail: drop_all.py drops the entire public schema and run_migrations.py applies all SQL files; both hardcode the DB password and connect to DB name `paybank_monolith` which no longer matches the current `noralpay` DB. They are footguns (schema drop) and broken, yet committed alongside leftover appsmith/ service config.
gaps.fix_direction: Remove drop_all.py, run_migrations.py, and appsmith/ from the repo (or move to a clearly isolated tooling dir with no hardcoded creds); rely on sqlx-cli for migrations.

gaps.title: Bare tracing subscriber: no JSON, no log-level filter
gaps.detail: tracing_subscriber::fmt::init() uses default human format and RUST_LOG-only filtering; the enabled `json` and `env-filter` features are unused. Production logs are unstructured (hard to ship/parse) and there is no explicit default level, so observability of payment flows is weak.
gaps.fix_direction: Build the subscriber with EnvFilter (sane default like info) and .json() in production, including target/span fields for correlation.

risks: Could not run the app or container, so the CWD-relative static-asset serving was assessed statically; behavior under a non-root user or changed WORKDIR is inferred, not observed.
Whether the committed provider keys are truly active vs. revoked sandbox keys was not verified against the providers; treated as P0 on the assumption they may be live.
sqlx migrate advisory-lock behavior means the multi-instance migration race is usually safe in practice; the concern is operational (coupling migrate to boot) more than data corruption.
Did not exhaustively read every route handler; observability/middleware assessment is based on the router definition and Cargo features, which is authoritative for layering.

designs.workstream: Authentication & Authorization (merchant API-key auth, admin JWT+roles, scoping of customer/webhook surfaces)
designs.approach:
The router (crates/paybank-api/src/router.rs:71-112) is a single flat Router with `.with_state(state)` and ZERO layers. AppState (crates/paybank-api/src/state.rs:1-10) holds only `db`. Auth is enforced today nowhere: merchant-api hardcodes DEMO_MERCHANT_ID (merchant_api.rs:11,51,104); admin handlers take only State+Query/Path/Json. Merchants already have a unique-indexed `api_key` TEXT column (migrations/001_initial_schema.sql:6,26) and an unused `password_hash` column (line 5). AppError already has the right variants: Unauthorized->401, AuthError(String)->401, MerchantNotFound->401 (error.rs:51-52,48-49,12-13,69,82). No JWT/bcrypt/argon crates are present yet. There is no admin_users table.

DESIGN: split the flat router into nested sub-routers and attach axum middleware via `from_fn_with_state` per surface, plus a global stack. Use three principals: (1) AuthedMerchant resolved from `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>` looked up against merchants.api_key (constant-time compare, status='active' gate); (2) AdminClaims from a signed admin JWT (HS256) carrying admin id + role, issued by a new POST /api/admin/login flow against an admin_users table; (3) public customer/webhook surfaces stay unauthenticated at the network layer but get a per-session bearer capability for money-moving actions and HMAC verification for webhooks. Inject the resolved principal as a request extension that handlers pull via an extractor, replacing DEMO_MERCHANT_ID and query-supplied merchant_id.

CONFIG: add a typed Config (JWT_SECRET, ADMIN_JWT_TTL, plus existing secrets) loaded at boot in src/main.rs and stored in an extended AppState { db, config } so middleware can read JWT_SECRET without per-request env reads. Add bcrypt (password hashing) and jsonwebtoken (HS256) to crates/paybank-api/Cargo.toml; subtle for constant-time api_key compare (or hash the key and compare digests).

MIDDLEWARE ORDER (outermost first): global layers go on the top Router AFTER nesting: TraceLayer (request-id) -> CorsLayer (allowlist admin origin, only needed if admin SPA is served cross-origin; same-origin today so restrict to credentials) -> DefaultBodyLimit -> per-surface auth middleware (innermost, closest to handler). Auth middleware MUST run before the handler but AFTER body-limit/trace so unauth requests are still logged and size-capped. Rate limiting (tower-governor) belongs outside auth on /login and /webhooks. Webhook HMAC verification stays INSIDE the handler (needs raw body bytes) and must NOT be wrapped by a JSON body extractor.
steps: 1. Add deps to crates/paybank-api/Cargo.toml: jsonwebtoken = "9", bcrypt = "0.15", subtle = "2". Add migrate feature usage stays in root crate. Optionally add tower-governor for rate limiting on /login and webhooks.

2. Extend Config: create crates/paybank-api/src/config.rs with `pub struct Config { pub jwt_secret: String, pub admin_jwt_ttl_secs: i64, pub merchant_api_key_pepper: Option<String> }` loaded via std::env::var with fail-fast at boot. Wire it in src/main.rs:13-23 (read JWT_SECRET, .expect) and pass into AppState.
3. Change AppState (crates/paybank-api/src/state.rs) to `pub struct AppState { pub db: Db, pub config: Arc<Config> }`; update AppState::new and the call in src/main.rs:23.

4. Create migration migrations/003_admin_users.sql: CREATE TABLE admin_users (id UUID PK default gen_random_uuid(), email TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, password_hash TEXT NOT NULL, role TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'viewer' CHECK (role IN ('superadmin','operator','viewer')), status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active', created_at, updated_at). Seed one superadmin via a SEPARATE non-migration step (do NOT bake a static password hash into a migration that runs in prod).

5. Add crates/paybank-db/src/admin_user_repo.rs: get_admin_by_email(pool,email)->Option<AdminUser> selecting id,email,password_hash,role,status; export from lib.rs. Add AdminUser model to paybank-core/src/models.rs (do NOT derive Serialize on password_hash, or add #[serde(skip_serializing)]).

6. Add crates/paybank-db/src/merchant_auth_repo.rs (or a function in admin_repo / new merchant_repo): get_merchant_by_api_key(pool, api_key)->Option<Merchant> with `WHERE api_key=$1 AND status='active'` using the existing idx_merchants_api_key. Constant-time compare is moot for an indexed exact lookup but keep status gating; longer term store sha256(api_key) and look up by hash prefix.

7. Create crates/paybank-api/src/auth.rs: (a) AuthedMerchant { merchant_id: Uuid, merchant: Merchant } extractor + `merchant_auth` middleware (axum::middleware::from_fn_with_state) that reads Authorization: Bearer, strips 'Bearer ', looks up via repo, on miss returns AppError::Unauthorized, on hit inserts AuthedMerchant into request extensions. (b) AdminClaims { sub: Uuid, role: AdminRole, exp } with Claims struct for jsonwebtoken; `admin_auth` middleware decoding the JWT from Authorization: Bearer (or HttpOnly cookie 'noor_admin') with Validation HS256 using state.config.jwt_secret, inserts AdminClaims into extensions; a `require_role(min)` helper. Implement axum FromRequestParts for AuthedMerchant and AdminClaims to pull from extensions.

8. Add admin login handlers in a new crates/paybank-api/src/routes/admin_auth.rs: POST /api/admin/login (LoginRequest{email,password}) -> verify bcrypt against admin_users.password_hash, on success issue HS256 JWT (sub=admin id, role, exp=now+ttl) and Set-Cookie HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite=Strict noor_admin, return {token, role}; POST /api/admin/logout clears cookie; GET /api/admin/me returns current AdminClaims. Rate-limit /login.

9. Restructure router.rs build_router into nested routers: admin_router (all /api/admin/* routes EXCEPT /login) layered with from_fn_with_state(state, admin_auth); merchant_router (all /api/merchant-api/* routes) layered with from_fn_with_state(state, merchant_auth); public_router (sessions read/stream/qr, /pay, /invoice, plaid, webhooks, banks, /health) with no auth layer. Mount /api/admin/login + /logout + /me on the admin_router pre-auth (login) / post-auth (me). nest them onto the top Router, then apply global layers (TraceLayer, DefaultBodyLimit::max, optional CorsLayer) and .with_state(state).

10. Replace DEMO_MERCHANT_ID usages: merchant_api.rs:51 and :104 take `merchant: AuthedMerchant` extractor and use merchant.merchant_id; get_balance (merchant_api.rs:21-24) drops the Path<merchant_id> and uses AuthedMerchant; remove the :merchant_id path param from router.rs:88 (balances become /api/merchant-api/balances). list_payments/create_payment_link scope to merchant.merchant_id.

11. Fix admin merchant leakage as part of authz hardening: change admin.rs list/get/create/update handlers to map Merchant -> a redacted DTO (reuse paybank-core MerchantResponse at models.rs:198-211 which omits password_hash; mask api_key to last-4 except on create). Add #[serde(skip_serializing)] to Merchant.password_hash (models.rs:155) as defense in depth. Gate create/update merchant behind require_role(operator+); reads allow viewer.

12. Scope customer money-movement: add a per-session capability secret. Add column payment_sessions.confirm_token TEXT (migration), set at create_session; require it as a bearer/path param on POST /api/sessions/:id/initiate and /confirm so a bare UUID cannot trigger transfers. Plaid exchange (plaid.rs:29-53) must also require the session confirm_token before mutating bank details. Session GET/stream stay public but switch to a non-PII projection (separate workstream owns the PII redaction).

13. Webhooks: leave on public_router but verify HMAC inside handler over raw Bytes (Column already does at webhooks.rs:22-41 — switch its compare to constant-time; MT must add HeaderMap + HMAC verify against MT secret). Do NOT add the merchant/admin auth layer to /api/webhooks/*.

14. Admin SPA gating (admin/src): add login() to admin/src/lib/api.ts that POSTs /api/admin/login and stores the JWT (in-memory + the HttpOnly cookie set by server). Change get()/post() (api.ts:115-136) to send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and `credentials:'include'`; on 401 redirect to a login view. Add admin/src/pages/Login.tsx and a top-level auth gate in admin/src/App.tsx (App.tsx:30) that renders Login until a valid token/me() succeeds, then renders the console; hide create/edit merchant controls when role==='viewer'. Drop api_key from the TS Merchant interface (api.ts:44).
can_parallelize_with: Payment Session Lifecycle (idempotency/state-machine) — but coordinate on sessions.rs/confirm.rs edits since this workstream adds the confirm_token gate there
Ledger & Balances (get_balance rewrite) — coordinate on merchant_api.rs get_balance signature change
Webhooks (MT signature verification) — this workstream only moves webhook routing into public_router; the HMAC verification body change is owned by the webhooks workstream
designs.test_plan: "Unit: merchant_auth middleware returns 401 on missing/garbage bearer, 401 for inactive/unknown api_key, injects correct merchant_id for valid key (use seeded merchant 0001 key pb_test_1234567890abcdef in test DB). admin_auth: 401 on absent/expired/wrong-signature JWT, 200 with valid token; require_role rejects viewer on create_merchant (403). bcrypt verify round-trip for login. Integration (http-body-util already a dev-dep in root Cargo.toml): hit /api/admin/stats without token -> 401; with token -> 200; /api/merchant-api/payments without bearer -> 401, with valid bearer -> scoped to that merchant only (assert a second merchant's transactions are NOT returned, i.e. cross-tenant isolation). Assert GET /api/admin/merchants response JSON has no password_hash field and api_key masked. POST /api/sessions/:id/initiate without confirm_token -> 401/403; with token -> proceeds. Webhook routes remain reachable without bearer (HMAC-gated). Frontend: manual — load /admin, confirm redirect to Login until login succeeds, confirm 401 on token expiry redirects back, confirm viewer role hides merchant create button."
designs.risk: "Splitting the flat router into nested routers can silently drop routes or break `with_state` typing (axum 0.7 nest + from_fn_with_state generics) — verify every one of the ~30 routes is still mounted and compiles. Adding the AuthedMerchant extractor to merchant_api handlers changes their signatures; the admin SPA's createSession() and initiateTransfer() (api.ts:161-181) currently call the PUBLIC /api/sessions surface, not merchant-api, so confirm which calls need a bearer vs session token to avoid breaking the console. The confirm_token gate on initiate touches the same handlers the lifecycle/idempotency workstream edits — merge conflicts and double-edits likely; sequence with that team. JWT_SECRET fail-fast at boot will break any env that lacks it (intended). Constant-time api_key compare is only meaningful if keys are hashed; storing plaintext keys (current schema) limits the benefit — flag the hash-at-rest follow-up. Moving webhooks under public_router must NOT accidentally inherit the global CORS/auth in a way that strips the raw body needed for HMAC."

designs.approach:
The pieces already exist but are disconnected. `IdempotencyRepo` (crates/paybank-db/src/idempotency_repo.rs:8-73) implements an insert-or-return-existing acquire (`try_acquire_key`, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING + re-SELECT, lines 18-51) and `complete_key` (lines 54-72) over the `idempotency_keys` table (migrations/001_initial_schema.sql:141-151, composite PK (merchant_id, idempotency_key), columns request_hash/response_status/response_body JSONB/state/expires_at). AppError ALREADY has MissingIdempotencyKey->400, IdempotencyMismatch->409, IdempotencyConflict->409, InvalidStateTransition->400 (crates/paybank-core/src/error.rs:30-37,74-77). So the contract was designed; nothing calls it. Both repo fns take a `&mut Transaction<'a, Postgres>`, but every route currently uses `&state.db.pool` directly (e.g. sessions.rs:46,154; confirm.rs:24,35; initiate.rs:17,46) and session_repo functions take `&PgPool`, NOT a tx. session_repo::update_status (session_repo.rs:56-75) is an unconditional UPDATE with no WHERE on prior status — not a CAS. There are TWO initiate endpoints (router.rs:77-79 JSON body, :83 path id) with divergent reference prefixes (txn_ vs pay_).

Design: introduce an Idempotency-Key HTTP header contract + per-endpoint request hash, wrap each money endpoint in ONE sqlx transaction that (1) acquires the key, (2) on first-seen does the work + a status CAS, (3) stores the canonical response, (4) commits. Retries with the same key+hash replay the stored response; same key+different hash -> 409 mismatch; concurrent in_progress -> 409 conflict. Defense in depth: pass the same logical key into the MT/Column provider call as a provider Idempotency-Key header so even a non-idempotent caller cannot double-pay at the provider. The merchant_id for the composite PK comes from session.merchant_id (looked up inside the tx) for confirm/initiate, and from req.merchant_id for create_session.

Scope decision: collapse the two initiate endpoints to one shared handler so the idempotency + CAS logic lives in exactly one place and the transaction reference is deterministic (derived from session id), so even without a header, the UNIQUE constraint on transactions.reference de-dupes.
steps: HEADER CONTRACT: Add an axum extractor `IdempotencyKey(String)` (FromRequestParts) that reads the `Idempotency-Key` header; if absent on a mutating money endpoint, return AppError::MissingIdempotencyKey (already 400 at error.rs:75). Require it on POST /api/sessions, /:id/confirm, /:id/initiate. Validate format (non-empty, <=255 chars, ASCII) to bound the TEXT PK. Document: clients MUST send a stable UUID/opaque token per logical attempt and reuse it verbatim on retry.

REQUEST HASH: Define a canonical request hash per endpoint = SHA-256 hex over (route discriminator + the semantically meaningful request fields). For create_session: merchant_id|bank_id|amount_cents|currency|note. For confirm: session_id|customer_name|address fields|account/routing (or the existing session bank fields). For initiate: session_id (the only input) plus amount_cents+rail_used read from the session, so a retry after the amount somehow changed is caught as a mismatch. Store this in idempotency_keys.request_hash via try_acquire_key (idempotency_repo.rs:15).

TRANSACTION BOUNDARY + ACQUIRE: At the top of each handler open `let mut tx = state.db.pool.begin().await?;`. Compute expires_at = now()+24h (mirror the session TTL). Call `IdempotencyRepo::try_acquire_key(&mut tx, merchant_id, &key, &request_hash, expires_at)`. Branch on the Result<Result<(),IdempotencyKey>,_>: Ok(Ok(())) => first-seen, proceed. Ok(Err(existing)) => key already present: if existing.request_hash != request_hash -> rollback, return AppError::IdempotencyMismatch (409). Else if existing.state=='completed' -> rollback, deserialize existing.response_body + response_status and REPLAY it verbatim (this is the retry-safe path). Else (state=='in_progress') -> rollback, return AppError::IdempotencyConflict (409) so the client retries later (provider call still in flight).

CONVERT session_repo TO ACCEPT A TX EXECUTOR: The blocker is that session_repo fns take &PgPool while IdempotencyRepo takes &mut Transaction. Refactor the session_repo functions used inside these handlers (create_session, get_session, update_status, update_counterparty_id, update_customer_details) plus transaction_repo::create_transaction to accept a generic `impl sqlx::PgExecutor` (or add `_tx` variants) so they can run on `&mut *tx`. This lets the idempotency row, session insert/update, counterparty store, and transactions insert all live in ONE atomic tx. Without this, the idempotency row and the money mutation are not atomic and a crash between them re-opens the double-submit window.

STATUS CAS (the actual double-pay fix): Replace the unconditional update_status (session_repo.rs:56-75) on the Processing transition with a conditional UPDATE inside the tx: `UPDATE payment_sessions SET status='processing', updated_at=NOW() WHERE id=$1 AND status='authorized' RETURNING id`. Use rows_affected()/fetch_optional: if 0 rows updated, the session was not in Authorized (already Processing/Completed/Expired) -> do NOT call the provider; return the current state (or AppError::InvalidStateTransition, 400, error.rs:74). Only when exactly 1 row flips to Processing do we proceed to initiate_transfer. This makes concurrent POSTs mutually exclusive at the DB even if they somehow share no idempotency key.

PROVIDER CALL OUTSIDE THE OUTER COMMIT WINDOW, KEYED: Do NOT hold the sqlx tx open across the 15s MT/Column HTTP call (it would pin a pool connection, only 10 in the pool per src/main.rs). Pattern: tx#1 acquires the idempotency key (state in_progress) AND does the Authorized->Processing CAS, then COMMIT. Then call paybank_payments::initiate_transfer, passing a deterministic provider idempotency key derived from the session id (e.g. the session UUID, or hash(session_id|attempt)). Then tx#2: on Ok set status Completed + insert transactions row with a deterministic reference `pay_{session_id}` (UNIQUE collides on retry) + complete_key(response 200, body); on Err mark for reconciliation (per audit, NOT blanket Expired) + complete_key with the error response. The in_progress row from tx#1 guards the gap: a concurrent retry sees in_progress -> 409 conflict.

THREAD PROVIDER IDEMPOTENCY KEY: Add an `idempotency_key: &str` param to paybank_payments::initiate_transfer (lib.rs:65) and to moderntreasury::create_transfer (moderntreasury.rs:151) / column::create_transfer. In MT, add `.header("Idempotency-Key", key)` to the /payment_orders POST (moderntreasury.rs:177-182) and /counterparties POST. Use the session UUID string as the stable key so a transport retry reuses the same MT payment order instead of creating a second. Do the same for create_counterparty (lib.rs:35 / confirm.rs:68 path).

COLLAPSE DUPLICATE INITIATE ENDPOINTS: Make routes/initiate.rs::initiate_session delegate to the same shared inner function as routes/sessions.rs::initiate_payment (router.rs:77-79 and :83), so reference prefix and recipient parsing cannot diverge. Use one deterministic transactions.reference = `pay_{session_id}` everywhere; the UNIQUE constraint then becomes a second de-dup layer.

REPLAY SERIALIZATION: The stored response_body must be the exact JSON the handler returns on success (e.g. {"status":"completed","transaction_id":...} for initiate; {"status":"authorized",...} for confirm; the CreateSessionResponse for create). On replay, return it with the stored response_status so retries are byte-identical. complete_key (idempotency_repo.rs:54) writes both.
depends_on: State-machine guard / SessionStatus terminal states (Failed/Returned/Reversed) workstream — the initiate Err path must NOT reuse Expired; idempotency replay of a failed attempt depends on a well-defined failure terminal.
can_parallelize_with: Auth layer (API-key/admin) — though auth provides the trusted merchant_id that idempotency keys are scoped to, so coordinate on how merchant_id is resolved for confirm/initiate (currently taken from the session row, which is fine pre-auth).
designs.test_plan: "There are zero tests in the workspace today, so add: (1) Unit test for the request-hash function: same inputs -> same hash, any field change -> different hash. (2) Integration test (sqlx against a test Postgres or mocked provider) for create_session: same Idempotency-Key + same body twice -> single session row, identical response; same key + different body -> 409 IdempotencyMismatch. (3) Initiate CAS test: seed an Authorized session, fire two concurrent initiate calls (tokio::join) with a stubbed initiate_transfer that counts invocations -> assert exactly ONE provider call and one transactions row; assert reference is `pay_{id}` from both endpoints. (4) Replay test: complete an initiate, retry with the same key -> byte-identical stored response, no second provider call. (5) In-progress conflict: hold tx#1 (in_progress) and fire a retry -> 409 IdempotencyConflict. (6) Provider key: assert moderntreasury::create_transfer sends an Idempotency-Key header equal to the session id (httpmock/wiremock). (7) Missing header -> 400 MissingIdempotencyKey."
designs.risk: "HIGH-leverage but touches the money path. Main risks: (a) Holding a sqlx tx across the 15s provider HTTP call would exhaust the 10-conn pool — the spec deliberately splits into tx#1 (acquire+CAS, commit) and tx#2 (finalize) with the in_progress row guarding the gap; getting this split wrong reopens the double-submit window. (b) Refactoring session_repo to a generic executor is broad and risks sqlx::query_as! macro/lifetime churn across many call sites. (c) merchant_id scoping: idempotency PK is (merchant_id, key); for confirm/initiate merchant_id comes from the session, so a key is only unique within a merchant — fine, but if a future auth layer supplies a different merchant_id the composite changes. (d) Replaying a stored FAILED response must align with the new Failed/Reconcile terminal states from the dependency workstream, not Expired. (e) The deterministic transactions.reference de-dup only helps if both endpoints converge on one prefix; leaving txn_ vs pay_ divergence (initiate.rs:82 vs sessions.rs:202) defeats it. (f) Ambiguous provider errors (timeout) must leave state reconcilable, not auto-complete the idempotency key as success."

designs.workstream: Ledger & Real Balances: wire double-entry postings into the payment lifecycle and compute real merchant balances
designs.approach:
Today nothing writes to the ledger and balances are a constant zero (merchant_api.rs:21-31). The repo already ships the right primitives: LedgerRepo::{create_journal_entry, create_posting, verify_balance, get_account} (ledger_repo.rs:8/28/52/83) all take a sqlx Transaction/Executor and are SQL-correct against migrations 001:106-139; an EntryType enum (models.rs:114-136) with exactly the lifecycle vocabulary needed (DebitPending, CreditPending, Settle, ReversePending, Refund, Fee, Payout) exists but is unused; and core::BalanceResponse (models.rs:390-395) already models available/pending/currency. The plan is: (1) define a per-merchant chart of accounts and provision it at merchant creation; (2) refactor the settlement write path so the transactions row + journal entry + two balanced postings + verify_balance happen in ONE sqlx transaction; (3) replace get_balance with a ledger aggregation that splits available vs pending by journal_entries.status; (4) add DB-level invariants.

ACCOUNT MODEL (per merchant, ledger_accounts.merchant_id NOT NULL for these). Reuse the 4 seed account NAMES already used for the demo merchant (002:40-45) so get_account(name, merchant_id) resolves: 'Receivables' (asset) = money owed by customer but not yet settled (pending inflow); 'Cash' (asset) = settled funds received; 'Settlement' (liability) = funds owed to the merchant for payout / available balance; 'Revenue' (revenue). The available/pending split is NOT modeled as two separate balances per account in this schema — instead derive it from journal_entries.status: postings under a 'pending' journal entry contribute to PENDING; postings under a 'posted' journal entry contribute to AVAILABLE. This requires one change: create_journal_entry currently hardcodes status='posted' (ledger_repo.rs:17); add a status parameter (or a second method create_pending_journal_entry) so the initiate-time entry is 'pending' and the settle-time entry/transition is 'posted'.

JOURNAL ENTRIES PER LIFECYCLE EVENT (all amounts = session.amount_cents, all balanced debit==credit):
- CONFIRM (authorize): no money has moved; write NO ledger postings. Authorization only links the counterparty (confirm.rs). Keep ledger empty here to avoid overstating receivables before initiation.
- INITIATE (transfer submitted to provider, on Ok of initiate_transfer): open ONE pending journal entry (status='pending', session_id=Some) representing the in-flight credit-pull: DEBIT Receivables, CREDIT Settlement for amount_cents. This makes the amount show up as PENDING in get_balance immediately on submission, which matches reality (funds requested, not yet cleared). Do NOT touch Cash yet, and do NOT set the session to Completed at this point (see settlement note).
- SETTLE (webhook settled/completed): transition the existing pending entry for that session to status='posted' (UPDATE journal_entries SET status='posted' WHERE session_id=$1 AND status='pending'), which atomically moves the amount from pending->available; AND write the transactions row. Net available balance now reflects settled funds. If a fee model is added later, post a Fee entry here (DEBIT Settlement, CREDIT Revenue) but that is out of scope for the first cut.
- RETURNED/REVERSED (webhook returned/reversed of a previously-settled payment): write a NEW compensating posted journal entry that reverses the settlement: DEBIT Settlement, CREDIT Receivables for amount_cents (mirror of the original), so the net ledger position returns to zero and the available balance is clawed back. This depends on the lifecycle workstream adding Returned/Reversed session states; until then, treat reversed as its own ledger reversal keyed off transfer_id idempotency.
- FAILED (provider definitively rejected at initiate, or failed webhook before settlement): if a pending entry was created, delete/void it by writing a reversing pending->voided transition (UPDATE journal_entries SET status='voided' WHERE session_id=$1 AND status='pending'); voided entries are excluded from both available and pending sums. No Cash/Revenue impact.

verify_balance USAGE: call LedgerRepo::verify_balance(&mut *tx, journal_entry_id) immediately after the two create_posting calls and BEFORE commit. It returns debits==credits && debits>0 (ledger_repo.rs:80). If false, roll the whole sqlx transaction back (return Err(AppError::Internal) / AppError::PaymentFailed) so the transactions row, journal entry, and postings are all-or-nothing. This is the application-level guarantee of the double-entry invariant.

REAL get_balance: rewrite merchant_api.rs:21-31 to query the ledger. available = SUM over ledger_postings p JOIN journal_entries j ON p.journal_entry_id=j.id JOIN ledger_accounts a ON p.account_id=a.id WHERE a.merchant_id=$1 AND a.name='Settlement' AND j.status='posted', signed as (credit - debit) because Settlement is a liability owed to the merchant; pending = same but j.status='pending'. Equivalent and simpler: available = (sum of credits to Settlement under posted entries) - (sum of debits to Settlement under posted entries). Use a single grouped query keyed on (j.status, p.direction). Return BalanceResponse with currency from the account row (default 'USD'). Note the merchant_api.rs:14 local BalanceResponse struct adds merchant_id; keep it or switch to core::BalanceResponse.

CRITICAL REFACTOR ENABLERS: transaction_repo::create_transaction currently takes &PgPool and self-executes (transaction_repo.rs:7-26) — it must be changed to accept &mut Transaction<Postgres> (or a generic Executor) so the row and the ledger postings commit atomically; same for any settlement helper. get_account takes a non-null Uuid (ledger_repo.rs:83) and ledger_accounts.merchant_id is nullable; since the chart of accounts is per-merchant here this is fine, but if platform/house accounts are later needed add a get_platform_account variant resolving WHERE merchant_id IS NULL.
steps: Add a status param to LedgerRepo::create_journal_entry (ledger_repo.rs:8) replacing the hardcoded 'posted' (line 17) with $3, OR add create_pending_journal_entry + a transition_entry_status helper (UPDATE journal_entries SET status=$2 WHERE session_id=$1 AND status='pending'). Keep verify_balance and create_posting as-is.

Add a ledger provisioning helper in ledger_repo (e.g. provision_merchant_accounts(tx, merchant_id)) that INSERTs the standard chart of accounts (Cash/asset, Receivables/asset, Revenue/revenue, Settlement/liability) for a merchant, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, mirroring the seed shape in migrations/002_seed_data.sql:40-45.

Call provision_merchant_accounts from admin_repo::create_merchant (admin_repo.rs:190-210) inside the same DB transaction as the merchant INSERT, so every new merchant gets a chart of accounts (currently only demo merchant 0001 has one).
Refactor transaction_repo::create_transaction (transaction_repo.rs:7-26) to take &mut sqlx::Transaction<'_, Postgres> instead of &PgPool so it can participate in the atomic settlement transaction.

Create a single settlement helper (e.g. ledger_repo::post_settlement or an api-layer function) that, inside one pool.begin() transaction: (a) resolves get_account(Receivables) and get_account(Settlement) for the merchant; (b) creates the journal entry; (c) create_posting DEBIT Receivables and CREDIT Settlement for amount_cents; (d) verify_balance and rollback if false; (e) writes the transactions row; (f) commits.

INITIATE wiring: in initiate.rs:64-90 and sessions.rs:184-205, on Ok(transfer) open a PENDING journal entry (DEBIT Receivables / CREDIT Settlement) inside the same tx that does the status update. Do NOT write the settled transactions row here if moving to webhook-driven settlement (see P2 finding); if keeping submit-time completion for now, write both pending entry and transaction atomically.

SETTLE wiring (webhooks.rs): on settled/completed, look up the session to get real merchant_id/amount/rail, then in one tx transition the pending journal entry to 'posted' AND write the transactions row (replacing the bogus Uuid::nil()/amount 0/FedNow insert at webhooks.rs:120-133). Make it idempotent on transfer_id (the transactions.reference UNIQUE on 'mt_{transfer_id}'/'pay_{session}' or an explicit dedupe). Stop using `let _ =` (webhooks.rs:122) so insert failures propagate.

RETURNED/REVERSED wiring (webhooks.rs:64-72, 109-113): on returned/reversed of a settled payment, write a compensating posted journal entry (DEBIT Settlement / CREDIT Receivables) so available balance is clawed back; gate on the lifecycle workstream adding distinct session states.

Rewrite get_balance (merchant_api.rs:21-31) to aggregate ledger_postings JOIN journal_entries JOIN ledger_accounts for the merchant's Settlement account: available = posted (credit-debit), pending = pending (credit-debit); return real BalanceResponse. Scope to the authenticated merchant once auth lands (currently uses path merchant_id).

Add a migration (003) with DB-level money-safety constraints: ledger_postings CHECK (direction IN ('debit','credit')), CHECK (amount_cents > 0); journal_entries.status CHECK IN ('pending','posted','voided'); a deferred constraint trigger asserting SUM(debit)=SUM(credit) per journal_entry_id; UNIQUE (merchant_id, name) on ledger_accounts to prevent duplicate roles.
depends_on: Lifecycle state-machine workstream (adds Returned/Reversed/Failed session states + CAS status transitions; the reversed/returned ledger entries and the move of settlement to webhook-time depend on these states existing)
Auth workstream (get_balance and ledger reads must be scoped to the authenticated merchant rather than a path/query merchant_id)
can_parallelize_with: Webhook signature verification work (MT HMAC) — touches webhooks.rs header parsing, not the ledger logic
Provider idempotency-key work in paybank-payments (moderntreasury.rs/column.rs) — separate crate, no ledger overlap
designs.test_plan: "Add unit/integration tests (none exist today): (1) provision_merchant_accounts creates exactly the 4 named accounts and is idempotent. (2) initiate posts a balanced PENDING entry: verify_balance returns true, get_balance shows pending=amount, available=0. (3) settlement transitions pending->posted: get_balance shows available=amount, pending=0, and exactly one transactions row exists (re-deliver the same webhook and assert no duplicate via the UNIQUE reference). (4) reversed webhook on a settled payment posts the compensating entry: get_balance returns to 0. (5) inject an unbalanced posting (debit!=credit) and assert verify_balance=false and the whole sqlx transaction rolls back (no transactions row, no postings persisted). (6) DB-level: assert the CHECK/trigger rejects amount_cents<=0, bad direction, and an unbalanced journal entry. (7) get_balance for a brand-new merchant with no postings returns 0/0/USD, not an error."
designs.risk: "Changing transaction_repo::create_transaction from &PgPool to a Transaction executor is an API break touching both initiate handlers and the MT webhook; all call sites must migrate together or the workspace won't compile. sqlx::query_as! macros are compile-time-checked against the DB, so the new status param and any new columns require DATABASE_URL/SQLX_OFFLINE cache to be regenerated (sqlx prepare). The pending-vs-posted-via-journal-status model is a design choice that couples balance semantics to journal_entries.status — if a later fee/payout flow needs finer-grained available/pending it may need dedicated sub-accounts; documented as a deliberate first-cut. The reversed-clawback path can drive available balance negative if a payout already occurred against it (no payout flow exists yet, so currently safe). Wiring settlement at webhook-time (correct) conflicts with the current submit-time Completed behavior; coordinate with the lifecycle workstream to avoid double-posting (one pending at initiate, one posted-transition at settle, never two postings)."

designs.workstream: PII Protection: stop storing raw bank account/routing numbers in plaintext (tokenize via Plaid processor_token / MT external_account_id; envelope-encrypt the residual that must persist)
designs.approach:
The raw DDA + routing numbers enter at exactly two write sites and live in two TEXT columns:

WRITE SITES
- Plaid link flow: routes/plaid.rs:36-52 takes accounts.first() from get_auth (plaid.rs:222-223 returns raw account_number/routing_number) and calls session_repo::update_customer_details (session_repo.rs:129-163), persisting into payment_sessions.customer_account_number / customer_routing_number (migrations/001:60-61, plain TEXT).
- Manual confirm flow: confirm.rs:35-50 re-writes the SAME raw values (read back from the session) via update_customer_details, then confirm.rs:52-72 builds a BankAccountDetails from the plaintext and calls create_counterparty.

READ/CONSUMER SITES (these need the cleartext only transiently, at counterparty-creation time)
- confirm.rs:57-68 -> paybank_payments::create_counterparty -> moderntreasury::create_counterparty (mt.rs:103-115 puts account_number/routing_number into the MT request) OR column::create_counterparty. After this call MT returns a durable external_account_id (lib.rs:41-46) that is the real long-term handle; raw numbers are never needed again for MT transfers (create_transfer uses receiving_account_id = the external account id, mt.rs:171).
- get_session / list_sessions (session_repo.rs:36-127) and admin_repo::list_all_sessions (admin_repo.rs:128-140) SELECT the two columns and serialize the full PaymentSession (models.rs:340-342) to API responses, including the unauthenticated admin SPA.

KEY INSIGHT: For the MT path the raw numbers are only needed for the single create_counterparty call; the MT external_account_id (already stored in column_counterparty_id as "cp_id|ext_id", confirm.rs:69) is a tokenized reference and is sufficient for all subsequent money movement. So the durable storage of raw PAN-equivalents is almost entirely unnecessary. The design is therefore two-pronged:

(1) TOKENIZE (preferred, eliminates storage): 
  - Plaid: switch from /auth/get (which returns raw account/routing) to the Plaid processor token flow — call /processor/token/create with processor "modern_treasury" (or "column") to get a processor_token, and feed THAT to MT/Column counterparty creation instead of raw numbers. Store only the processor_token + masked last-4. This removes raw numbers from the system entirely on the Plaid path. (Requires the MT<->Plaid or Column<->Plaid processor integration to be enabled in the Plaid dashboard.)
  - Result handle: persist the MT external_account_id / Column counterparty id as the canonical pay-to reference (already partially done in column_counterparty_id). Store a non-reversible mask (last-4 of account, last-4 of routing) for display.

(2) ENVELOPE-ENCRYPT THE RESIDUAL (for the manual-entry path and any case where a processor token is not yet available and the raw value must round-trip until counterparty creation):
  - Application-level envelope encryption: a 256-bit data encryption key (DEK) encrypts each field with AES-256-GCM; the DEK is itself encrypted by a KMS-held key-encryption-key (KEK). Store ciphertext + nonce + wrapped-DEK + key version. Decrypt only in the create_counterparty code path, never in list/get read paths.
  - Crate choice: add `aes-gcm = "0.10"` and `rand = "0.8"` to paybank-db (or a new paybank-crypto crate). `base64` is already a dep in paybank-payments; `hmac`/`sha2` already in paybank-api. No AEAD crate exists yet, so it must be added.

This avoids inventing a Payment table (models.rs:213-248 Payment is dead/unbacked) and works with the existing payment_sessions row.
steps: DECIDE STORAGE MODEL: Adopt tokenize-first. Default path = Plaid processor_token -> provider counterparty; raw numbers never persisted. Manual-entry path = envelope-encrypted-at-rest until counterparty creation, then zeroed.

SCHEMA (new migration 003_pii_protection.sql): (a) Add columns to payment_sessions: customer_account_number_enc BYTEA, customer_routing_number_enc BYTEA, pii_nonce BYTEA, pii_wrapped_dek BYTEA, pii_key_version INT, customer_account_last4 TEXT, customer_routing_last4 TEXT, plaid_processor_token_enc BYTEA (+ its own nonce/wrapped-dek if stored separately), provider_external_account_id TEXT (promote the ext-id half out of the overloaded column_counterparty_id 'cp|ext' string). (b) Do NOT drop customer_account_number/customer_routing_number yet — keep them for the dual-read backfill window; mark for removal in a later migration. (c) Add CHECK/length on last4 columns.

CRYPTO MODULE: Add a paybank-crypto module (or fn block in paybank-db) implementing: encrypt_field(plaintext) -> {ciphertext, nonce, wrapped_dek, key_version} using AES-256-GCM with a per-field random 96-bit nonce and a per-row random DEK; wrap the DEK with the KEK. decrypt_field(...) reverses it. Bind associated-data (AAD) = session_id||field_name to prevent ciphertext swapping between fields/rows.

KEY MANAGEMENT: KEK lives in a KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Vault transit). Two acceptable implementations: (i) Real KMS Encrypt/Decrypt of the DEK on each operation (add aws-sdk-kms); (ii) Bootstrap fallback for non-cloud: a single 32-byte master KEK loaded at startup from env (KEK_MASTER_KEY, base64) into the typed Config (the audit recommends a startup Config struct), wrapping the DEK locally. key_version column enables rotation: new rows use the latest KEK; decrypt selects KEK by version. NEVER read the KEK ad hoc via env at call time — load once at boot, fail fast if missing.

PLAID WRITE PATH (plaid.rs + routes/plaid.rs): Replace get_auth (which returns raw numbers) usage with a processor-token call: after exchange_public_token, call a new create_processor_token(access_token, account_id, processor) -> processor_token. In routes/plaid.rs:36-52, persist the processor_token (encrypted) + last-4 (from a balances/identity call or Plaid's masked account 'mask' field) instead of raw account/routing. Stop returning raw numbers in the HTTP response (plaid.rs / routes/plaid.rs:55-57) — return only account_name, mask/last4, subtype. Propagate the DB write error (replace `let _ =` at plaid.rs:37).

CONFIRM/MANUAL WRITE PATH (confirm.rs + session_repo.rs): When raw numbers are supplied manually, encrypt them via the crypto module before storing (write *_enc + nonce + wrapped_dek + key_version + last4). Update update_customer_details (session_repo.rs:129-163) to accept the encrypted blobs + last4 instead of raw account_number/routing_number, OR add a new update_customer_bank_details_encrypted fn. Stop the placeholder email/phone overwrite at confirm.rs:39-40 (separate finding) so this path doesn't also corrupt PII.

COUNTERPARTY CREATION (confirm.rs:52-72, lib.rs:35-63): Decrypt the raw numbers (or pass the processor_token) ONLY here, in-memory, immediately before create_counterparty. For the processor-token path, switch MT/Column counterparty creation to accept a processor_token (MT supports creating an external account from a Plaid processor token) instead of raw account_details/routing_details (mt.rs:103-115). Persist the returned external_account_id into the new provider_external_account_id column. After successful counterparty creation, optionally NULL out the *_enc raw columns (the durable handle is now the provider token).

READ PATH HARDENING (session_repo.rs:36-127, admin_repo.rs:128-140): Remove customer_account_number / customer_routing_number from every SELECT that feeds a serialized response. Replace the PaymentSession struct fields (models.rs:340-342) so the API model carries only customer_account_last4 / customer_routing_last4, never the raw or even encrypted blobs. The encrypted blobs are read only by an internal repo fn used by the counterparty path. Add #[serde(skip_serializing)] defense-in-depth on any residual sensitive field.

MIGRATION OF EXISTING ROWS (one-off backfill, run as a job not at app boot): For each payment_sessions row with non-null customer_account_number/customer_routing_number: encrypt the value into *_enc/nonce/wrapped_dek/key_version, derive last4, then UPDATE; in the same statement set the plaintext columns to NULL. designs.workstream: Failure / Returns / Reversals handling: distinct terminal states, webhook-driven Returned/Reversed/Refunded, and ledger reversal entries
designs.approach:
Today every failure path collapses into `SessionStatus::Expired`: transfer-Err in both initiate handlers (initiate.rs:96, sessions.rs:213), and provider webhooks mapping failed/returned/reversed -> Expired (webhooks.rs:64-72 Column, webhooks.rs:108-113 MT). `SessionStatus` (models.rs:103-109) has only Pending/Authorized/Processing/Completed/Expired and no terminal failure states, so a clawed-back settled payment is indistinguishable from an unused expired link, and a `reversed` webhook silently flips Completed->Expired with NO compensating ledger entry. Meanwhile `PaymentStatus` (models.rs:51-61) ALREADY defines Failed/Returned/Reversed/Refunded and `EntryType` (models.rs:114-122) already defines ReversePending/Refund — these are the intended vocabulary, just never wired to sessions.

The fix has four parts, all grounded in existing scaffolding:

(1) STATE MODEL: Extend `SessionStatus` with Failed, Returned, Reversed, Refunded (mirroring the existing PaymentStatus variants and their snake_case sqlx mapping at models.rs:100-102). Add a migration 003 with a CHECK constraint on payment_sessions.status enumerating the legal string set (currently unconstrained TEXT per the schema audit). Keep `Expired` meaning ONLY 'link timed out, never funded'.

(2) STATE MACHINE + CAS ENFORCEMENT in session_repo.rs: `update_status` (session_repo.rs:56-75) is an unconditional `UPDATE ... WHERE id=$1` — replace with transition-guarded UPDATEs that name the allowed source states in the WHERE clause and RETURN the row, so callers can detect rowcount==0 (illegal/duplicate transition). Legal edges: Pending->Authorized->Processing; Processing->{Completed,Failed}; Completed->{Returned,Reversed}; Returned/Reversed->Refunded; {Pending,Authorized}->Expired. Never allow downgrade out of Completed except to Returned/Reversed; never resurrect a terminal Failed/Expired. This single chokepoint is where the machine is enforced for BOTH initiate handlers and BOTH webhook handlers.

(3) INITIATE FAILURE SEMANTICS (initiate.rs:92-101, sessions.rs:212-215): stop writing Expired on transfer-Err. Classify the error from initiate_transfer: a definitive provider rejection (4xx with a parsed reject body from moderntreasury.rs:184/column.rs:172) -> set Failed via CAS from Processing; an AMBIGUOUS error (15s timeout, connection reset, 5xx — currently all flattened into ModernTreasuryError/ColumnError strings) -> LEAVE status Processing (do NOT touch it) and let webhook/poller reconcile, because MT may have actually created the order. designs.approach:
The repo has zero tests and a structure that is hostile to testing the money paths as-is. Two facts drive the entire strategy and must be acknowledged up front:

(1) NO PROVIDER TRAIT EXISTS and base URLs are hard `const`s (crates/paybank-payments/src/moderntreasury.rs:9 MT_BASE_URL, column.rs:9 COLUMN_BASE_URL, plaid.rs:5 PLAID_BASE_URL). The money functions are free functions in crates/paybank-payments/src/lib.rs (create_counterparty:35, initiate_transfer:65, check_transfer_status:115) that dispatch on PaymentProvider::primary() (lib.rs:18-27, env-gated) and call module functions that build a fresh reqwest::Client to a const URL. Route handlers (initiate.rs:54, sessions.rs:174, confirm.rs) call paybank_payments::* directly, NOT through AppState (state.rs is just {db: Db{pool}}). Therefore handler-level integration tests CANNOT substitute a mock provider without a code change. The task asks for "provider trait + mock impls"; delivering that requires a small, test-enabling refactor that is itself part of this workstream (see steps). I recommend the minimal version: make the three base URLs read from env with the current value as default (e.g. MT_BASE_URL via std::env::var(\"MT_BASE_URL\").unwrap_or(\"https://app.moderntreasury.com/api\")), which lets tests point the real client code at a wiremock server and exercise the genuine request/response (de)serialization — strictly better than a hand-rolled trait mock for catching the audit's serde/HTTP-status bugs (moderntreasury.rs:206 no status check; column.rs:106,191 no status check; plaid.rs no error_for_status). A `PaymentProvider` trait can be added on top for pure-unit handler tests, but env+wiremock is the higher-value primary lever and the only way to test the actual provider serialization that the audit flagged as speculative.

(2) DB repos use sqlx::query_as!/query! compile-time-checked macros (session_repo.rs, idempotency_repo.rs, etc.). These require either a live DATABASE_URL at compile time OR a committed .sqlx offline cache (SQLX_OFFLINE=true is already used in the Dockerfile per the ops audit). So ALL test compilation already depends on the offline cache or a DB. DB-backed tests must therefore hit a real ephemeral Postgres — there is no in-memory substitute for sqlx-pg. Use one disposable Postgres (testcontainers-rs OR a CI service container) seeded by sqlx::migrate!(\"./migrations\") run against a fresh database-per-test (or per-test schema/txn rollback) for isolation.
