designs.workstream: Observability & Audit Log (structured JSON tracing + request IDs, immutable audit log, Prometheus metrics, Sentry error tracking)
designs.approach:
Replace the bare `tracing_subscriber::fmt::init()` (src/main.rs:11) with a layered Registry: EnvFilter (default "info,paybank=debug", honoring RUST_LOG), a JSON fmt layer (the `json`/`env-filter` features are ALREADY enabled in Cargo.toml:25 but unused), a Sentry tracing layer, and a metrics layer. Add a tower-http TraceLayer + request-id propagation onto build_router (router.rs:71-112) — note tower-http is already compiled with the `trace` feature (paybank-api/Cargo.toml:16) but ZERO layers are currently applied. Three observability planes:

1) STRUCTURED LOGGING + REQUEST IDs: A `SetRequestIdLayer`/`PropagateRequestIdLayer` (x-request-id, generate UUID if absent) wrapped by a `TraceLayer::new_for_http()` whose `make_span_with` opens a span carrying method, matched route (axum's MatchedPath, NOT raw uri — raw uri leaks session UUIDs/PII into logs), and request_id. on_response logs status + latency_ms. All existing `tracing::info!`/`tracing::error!` calls (webhooks.rs:101,117; error.rs:84,88; main.rs:28) then emit as JSON with the request_id field automatically attached via span context. CRITICAL money-safety constraint for THIS repo: the JSON layer must never serialize PaymentSession/BankAccountDetails/Merchant — those carry plaintext account_number/routing_number (migrations/001:60-61) and password_hash/api_key (001:5-6). Forbid logging whole structs; log only ids + masked last-4.

2) IMMUTABLE AUDIT LOG: New `audit_log` table (append-only) written from a new `paybank_db::audit_repo`. Audit is SEPARATE from access logs (TraceLayer) — it records business facts (who did what to which money object), survives log rotation, and is queryable. Every money-moving and admin mutation gets an explicit `audit_repo::record(...)` call inside the same sqlx transaction as the state change so the audit row is atomic with the effect (can't have a transfer without its audit row, can't have an audit row for a rolled-back transfer). Writes are INSERT-only; no UPDATE/DELETE path is exposed and DB privileges should revoke them.

3) METRICS (Prometheus): `metrics` + `metrics-exporter-prometheus` crates; a recorder installed in main, a GET /metrics route (no auth needed for scrape but should be bound internal-only / behind the reverse proxy), and counters/histograms incremented at money-movement points.

4) SENTRY: `sentry` + `sentry-tower` + `sentry-tracing`. Init guard in main (DSN from env; no-op if unset so dev/sandbox is unaffected). A `SentryHttpLayer` + `NewSentryLayer` on the router to scope each request, and the sentry-tracing layer so `tracing::error!` events (already emitted from error.rs:84,88 for Database/Internal) become Sentry events. Must scrub PII via before_send.

AppState (state.rs:2-4) currently holds only `db`. It must gain the Prometheus handle (for /metrics) and optionally a typed Config; since handlers already have State(state), audit writes go through state.db.pool. No new field strictly required for audit beyond the pool, but adding actor/request-id propagation into handlers needs an extractor or Extension.
steps: MIGRATION 003_audit_log.sql: CREATE TABLE audit_log (id UUID PK DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), occurred_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), request_id TEXT, actor_type TEXT NOT NULL (system|merchant|admin|customer|provider_webhook), actor_id TEXT, action TEXT NOT NULL, object_type TEXT NOT NULL, object_id UUID, merchant_id UUID, session_id UUID, amount_cents BIGINT, prev_status TEXT, new_status TEXT, provider TEXT, provider_ref TEXT, ip TEXT, outcome TEXT NOT NULL (success|failure|denied), metadata JSONB, hash TEXT). Add CHECK constraints on actor_type/outcome. Indexes on (session_id), (merchant_id, occurred_at DESC), (action, occurred_at DESC), (object_id). Append-only: do NOT add updated_at; add a comment and plan a DB role that has INSERT+SELECT only. Optional tamper-evidence: hash = sha256(prev_hash || row-canonical-json) chained per (object_id) for an immutable audit trail.

Create crates/paybank-db/src/audit_repo.rs with `record(executor, AuditEntry)` taking a generic `impl sqlx::PgExecutor` so it works with both &PgPool and &mut Transaction (so audit rows commit atomically with money-state changes). Define a builder/struct AuditEntry mirroring the columns. Add `audit_log` queries: list_by_session, list_by_merchant for the admin UI. Export from crates/paybank-db/src/lib.rs:1-7 (add `pub mod audit_repo;`).

Add an `AuditEntry` / `AuditAction` enum + an `Actor` struct to paybank-core/src/models.rs near the existing enums (SessionStatus models.rs:100-109). Actions to model: SessionCreated, SessionConfirmed, CounterpartyCreated, TransferInitiated, TransferSubmitted, TransferSucceeded, TransferFailed, SessionStatusChanged(prev,new), WebhookReceived, WebhookVerifyFailed, MerchantCreated, MerchantUpdated, BankLinked. These map 1:1 to the audit points below.

Rewrite tracing init in src/main.rs:6,11. Build a tracing_subscriber::registry().with(EnvFilter::try_from_default_env().unwrap_or(EnvFilter::new("info,paybank=debug"))).with(fmt::layer().json().with_current_span(true).with_span_list(false)).with(sentry_tracing::layer()).with(MetricsLayer). Install BEFORE reading any env so config-load failures are logged. Keep the existing info!("Depost API starting") (main.rs:28) — it now emits JSON.

Add observability middleware stack to build_router (router.rs:71). Layer order (outermost first): NewSentryLayer + SentryHttpLayer (scope per request), PropagateRequestIdLayer + SetRequestIdLayer(x-request-id, MakeRequestUuid), TraceLayer::new_for_http().make_span_with(closure capturing method + MatchedPath + request_id; NEVER req.uri() full path). Add a separate `.route("/metrics", get(metrics_handler))` returning the Prometheus text exposition. Keep /health (router.rs:73) and add /ready (SELECT 1) — observability needs a real readiness signal. Do NOT put TraceLayer over the SSE stream route (sessions.rs stream) in a way that logs per-poll; or accept that.

Install Prometheus recorder in main: let handle = PrometheusBuilder::new().install_recorder()?; store handle in AppState (extend state.rs:2-4 with `pub metrics: PrometheusHandle`). metrics_handler returns handle.render(). Define metric names: noor_http_requests_total{route,method,status}, noor_http_request_duration_seconds (histogram), noor_transfer_initiated_total{provider,rail}, noor_transfer_succeeded_total{provider,rail}, noor_transfer_failed_total{provider,rail,reason}, noor_webhook_received_total{provider,verified}, noor_session_status_transition_total{from,to}, noor_money_moved_cents_total{provider,rail} (monotonic counter of amount), noor_db_pool_in_use (gauge). Increment HTTP metrics from the TraceLayer on_response; increment business metrics at the audit points.

Init Sentry in main BEFORE tokio runtime if possible (sentry guard must outlive main): let _guard = sentry::init((dsn, ClientOptions { release: env!CARGO_PKG_VERSION, environment: from env, traces_sample_rate: low, before_send: scrub_pii, ..default })). DSN read from SENTRY_DSN; if absent, skip init (no-op) so sandbox/dev is unaffected. Add a before_send/before_breadcrumb that strips request bodies and any field named account_number/routing_number/api_key/password_hash/secret. Tie into error.rs:83-90: the Database/Internal arms already tracing::error! — with sentry_tracing::layer() those auto-capture; optionally add explicit sentry::capture_error in those arms for richer context.

WIRE AUDIT POINTS — money movement (P0 importance, do inside the same DB tx as the effect). (a) initiate.rs:46-100 and sessions.rs initiate_payment (the TWO duplicate initiate endpoints): emit TransferInitiated before calling paybank_payments::initiate_transfer (initiate.rs:54), TransferSucceeded with provider+provider_transfer_id on Ok (initiate.rs:64), TransferFailed with the error string + whether definite/ambiguous on Err (initiate.rs:92). Record amount_cents, rail, merchant_id, session_id. (b) confirm.rs counterparty creation + status->Authorized: emit CounterpartyCreated and SessionStatusChanged. (c) session_repo::update_status (session_repo.rs:56-75): the cleanest single chokepoint — change its signature to also accept an Actor + reason and write an audit row in the SAME query/tx, so EVERY status transition (including the webhook-driven ones at webhooks.rs:56,65,74,116) is audited with prev->new. This also captures the lazy-expiry and webhook transitions the lifecycle audit flagged.

WIRE AUDIT POINTS — webhooks (webhooks.rs). column_webhook: on signature mismatch (webhooks.rs:35) record WebhookVerifyFailed outcome=denied + increment noor_webhook_received_total{provider=column,verified=false}; on success record WebhookReceived with provider status string and the resulting transition. moderntreasury_webhook (webhooks.rs:89-137, currently UNVERIFIED): once signature verification is added by the webhooks workstream, record WebhookReceived/WebhookVerifyFailed identically. Audit must capture the raw provider event_type+status even when no session matches (the silent-no-op case the webhook audit flagged), so unmatched events are visible.

WIRE AUDIT POINTS — admin actions (admin.rs). create_merchant (admin.rs:105-117): record MerchantCreated actor_type=admin (actor_id from the future admin-auth principal — until auth exists, record actor_id='UNAUTHENTICATED' so the gap is visible in the audit trail rather than silently absent). update_merchant (admin.rs:119-137): record MerchantUpdated with a metadata diff of changed fields (business_name/tax_id/webhook_url — webhook_url changes are security-sensitive: redirecting webhook delivery). These are the 'admin action' half of the audit requirement.

Add audit/observability config to a typed Config (aligns with the build/ops workstream's fail-fast config): SENTRY_DSN, SENTRY_ENVIRONMENT, RUST_LOG default, METRICS_BIND/enable. Read at startup, not per-request. Document in .env.example. Ensure /metrics and Sentry are opt-in via env so they don't break local runs.

Tests: unit test audit_repo::record round-trips and is queryable; test that update_status writes exactly one audit row per transition; test the tracing JSON layer does not serialize a PaymentSession (compile-time: provide a Display/redacted impl, or a test that the log line for a session contains only last-4). Add a test asserting /metrics renders and increments noor_transfer_* after a mocked initiate. (Repo currently has ZERO tests — this establishes the harness.)
depends_on: AUTH & SECURITY surface (admin/merchant/customer auth) — the audit log needs a real authenticated actor_id; until auth lands, audit records actor_id as UNAUTHENTICATED, which is a placeholder, not the end state
Payment Session Lifecycle (CAS state transitions + Failed/Returned/Reversed states) — auditing update_status is most valuable once it is a conditional transition and the status enum is complete
BUILD/OPS typed Config + fail-fast secrets — Sentry DSN / metrics config should come from the central Config, not scattered std::env::var
can_parallelize_with: Ledger & Balances (double-entry wiring) — the ledger transaction is a natural place to also emit an audit row, but the two can be built independently
designs.test_plan: "1) cargo build to confirm the new tracing/Sentry/metrics layers compile with the already-enabled json/env-filter features. 2) Run the API with RUST_LOG unset and confirm logs emit as single-line JSON with request_id, method, matched route, status, latency_ms; confirm a request to /api/sessions/:id does NOT log the full session (no account_number/routing_number in output). 3) curl /metrics and confirm Prometheus exposition renders; POST a (mocked) initiate and confirm noor_transfer_initiated_total / noor_money_moved_cents_total increment. 4) Insert via audit_repo and SELECT to confirm append-only rows with request_id/actor/action/prev_status/new_status; drive a session through create->confirm->initiate->webhook and assert one audit row per transition with correct prev->new. 5) Set SENTRY_DSN to a test/relay DSN, force an AppError::Internal, confirm an event arrives with PII scrubbed (no body, no account numbers). 6) Unset SENTRY_DSN and confirm startup + requests still work (no-op). 7) Confirm signature-mismatch on the Column webhook records a WebhookVerifyFailed/denied audit row and increments noor_webhook_received_total{verified=false}. Unit tests in crates/paybank-db for audit_repo and crates/paybank-api for the redaction guarantee."
designs.risk: "PII leakage via logs/Sentry is the dominant risk: this repo logs and serializes structs that contain plaintext bank account/routing numbers (PaymentSession, BankAccountDetails) and merchant secrets (password_hash, api_key) — the new JSON layer and Sentry capture must be built with redaction from the start or observability becomes a new exfiltration channel. Routing the audit write through session_repo::update_status changes a widely-called signature (called in initiate.rs, sessions.rs, confirm.rs, webhooks.rs x4) — must update all call sites; mitigated by the type checker. Audit immutability is only as strong as DB grants — the table is append-only by convention; without a restricted DB role (INSERT/SELECT only) an attacker with DB access can still tamper, and the optional hash-chain is the real tamper-evidence. /metrics must not be publicly exposed (cardinality DoS via route labels is bounded since we use MatchedPath not raw uri, but it can leak internal volume). Sentry sample rate + before_send misconfiguration could either drop money-movement errors or leak PII. TraceLayer over the SSE stream route (sessions.rs:104-148) could spam logs on every 2s poll. Adding sentry/metrics/tower-http layers grows the dependency tree and build time."

designs.approach:
Build a GitHub Actions pipeline plus harden the container/compose for THIS repo. Ground truths verified: cargo workspace with bin `paybank` at src/main.rs (root Cargo.toml), 5 member crates, edition 2021, no rust-toolchain pin. A committed `.sqlx/` offline cache exists (21 query JSON files) and `.sqlx/` is gitignored-as-dir-contents-but-files-are-tracked — Dockerfile already builds with `SQLX_OFFLINE=true cargo build --release --bin paybank`, so CI can run offline too. Admin SPA is Vite (admin/package.json: `tsc -b && vite build`, node 22, npm ci). Dockerfile is 3-stage (node:22-alpine -> rust:1-slim-bookworm -> debian:bookworm-slim) but the runtime stage runs as ROOT, has no WORKDIR, no HEALTHCHECK, and serves CWD-relative assets (router.rs:14-16,22-24 read `web/pay.html`/`web/invoice.html`; ServeDir::new("web") and `/admin/dist` static), which only resolve because CWD=`/` and assets are COPYed to `/web` and `/admin/dist`. EXPOSE 8888 but code default BIND_ADDR is 0.0.0.0:3000 (main.rs:25). docker-compose.yml hardcodes live-format provider secrets (lines 29-37) and appsmith/docker-compose.yml hardcodes encryption secrets. drop_all.py + run_migrations.py are git-tracked, hardcode the DB password, and point at stale DB `paybank_monolith` (current is `noralpay`). migrations run at boot via sqlx::migrate! (main.rs:20).

PIPELINE DESIGN (.github/workflows/ci.yml): one workflow, jobs keyed to the toolchain. (1) `fmt`: cargo fmt --all --check. (2) `clippy`: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, with SQLX_OFFLINE=true so the macro checks use .sqlx. (3) `sqlx-prepare-check`: spin up a postgres service container, run the migrations against it via sqlx migrate run (replacing the boot-time auto-migrate as the source of truth), then `cargo sqlx prepare --workspace --check` to assert the committed .sqlx cache matches the live schema — this is the regression guard for the offline cache. (4) `test`: cargo test --workspace (tests/ dir currently empty but wire it now). (5) `admin-build`: node 22, `npm ci` + `npm run build` in admin/, upload dist artifact. (6) `docker-build`: build the hardened image with buildx + GHA layer cache; on push to main also build/push tagged. (7) `security`: cargo-audit + cargo-deny + gitleaks (the compose secrets finding makes secret scanning load-bearing). Use Swatinem/rust-cache for target caching; pin actions by tag.

DOCKERFILE HARDENING: keep 3-stage, but in the runtime stage add a non-root user (useradd --system --uid 10001 noor), set WORKDIR /app and COPY assets to /app/web and /app/admin/dist so CWD-relative reads still resolve and are no longer coupled to `/`; add HEALTHCHECK hitting the new readiness endpoint (curl/wget against http://127.0.0.1:8888/health); switch base to gcr.io/distroless/cc-debian12 if feasible (binary is dynamically linked to openssl/libssl per builder apt install — distroless cc includes libssl) OR keep debian:bookworm-slim with only ca-certificates; set USER 10001; align EXPOSE/CMD with BIND_ADDR=0.0.0.0:8888. Pin builder to a concrete rust version (add rust-toolchain.toml) so CI and Docker agree.

MIGRATIONS AS GATED DEPLOY STEP: remove sqlx::migrate! from boot (main.rs:20) behind an env flag (RUN_MIGRATIONS=true) defaulting to false; make migrations a discrete step — a `migrate` service/profile in compose (one-shot, runs `sqlx migrate run` then exits) and a dedicated CI/CD deploy job that runs migrations once before rolling new API replicas. This removes the multi-instance boot race and gives an auditable gate.

COMPOSE HARDENING: move all provider secrets out of docker-compose.yml into an untracked `.env` referenced via `env_file:` (or compose `secrets:`); add an `api` healthcheck; add a one-shot `migrate` service depending on postgres healthy; keep `restart: unless-stopped`. Rotate the exposed keys (out of scope to do here but called out). 

CRUFT REMOVAL: git rm appsmith/, drop_all.py, run_migrations.py (the audit's P3); they are footguns (schema drop, stale DB name, hardcoded creds) and appsmith leaks secrets. .dockerignore already excludes appsmith/ and .env (good) but the files remain in git history.
steps: Add rust-toolchain.toml at repo root pinning channel = "1.XX" (a concrete stable, matching what crates compile under) and components rustfmt+clippy, so CI, local, and Docker builder agree on a version instead of the floating rust:1-slim-bookworm tag.
Create .github/workflows/ci.yml. Job `fmt`: actions/checkout, dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable (or read rust-toolchain.toml), run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`.
Same workflow Job `clippy`: checkout, toolchain with clippy, Swatinem/rust-cache, env SQLX_OFFLINE=true, run `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`.
Job `test`: checkout, toolchain, rust-cache, env SQLX_OFFLINE=true, run `cargo test --workspace --all-features`. (tests/ is currently empty — this gate exists for when ledger/rail tests land.)

Add a one-shot `migrate` service to docker-compose.yml using the same image with command running `sqlx migrate run` (or the binary with RUN_MIGRATIONS=true) depending_on postgres healthy; document it as the gated deploy step. Add a CI/CD deploy job that runs migrations once before rolling API instances.

Rewrite docker-compose.yml: replace inline provider secrets (lines 29-37) with `env_file: .env` (untracked) or compose `secrets:`; add an `api` `healthcheck` (wget /health); align BIND_ADDR/PUBLIC_APP_URL; keep postgres healthcheck.
Set BIND_ADDR default in main.rs:25 to 0.0.0.0:8888 (or require it explicitly) so the code default matches EXPOSE/compose 8888.

Remove cruft from git: `git rm -r appsmith/`, `git rm drop_all.py run_migrations.py`; rely on sqlx-cli for migrations. Note these (and any real keys in docker-compose.yml history) require git-history scrubbing + key rotation, called out as follow-up.

designs.approach:
The admin SPA (admin/src) today renders `<App/>` unconditionally from main.tsx with zero auth, and every admin data call funnels through two private helpers `get`/`post` in admin/src/lib/api.ts:115-136 using bare `fetch` with only `Content-Type` (no Authorization, no credentials). That single chokepoint is the lever: attach a token there and centralize 401 handling there. Three session-action calls (`createSession` api.ts:168, `initiateTransfer` api.ts:178, `fetchQrSvg` api.ts:184) bypass those helpers and hit the public /api/sessions surface — they must be routed through a shared authed-fetch wrapper too, or at least carry the token, since the aligned backend will gate session actions behind admin auth.

Design a token-based gate that matches the backend admin-auth workstream (which exposes POST /api/admin/login -> {token, operator:{id,name,email,role}}, GET /api/admin/me for token validation/operator hydration, and returns 401 on missing/expired/invalid bearer for every /api/admin/* route). The frontend keeps the bearer token in memory + localStorage, hydrates an AuthContext on boot by validating the stored token against /api/admin/me, shows a LoginScreen when unauthenticated, attaches `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to every request via the api.ts helpers, and on any 401 clears the token and bounces back to the login screen (instead of the current behavior where a 401 surfaces as a raw red error flash on each page via useAsync.ts:17).

Concretely: (1) add a typed auth module + React context that owns token/operator state and login/logout; (2) refactor api.ts so `get`/`post` (and the three stray fetch helpers) pull the token from the auth module and throw a tagged UnauthorizedError on 401; (3) register a single 401 callback from the context into the api module so a 401 anywhere triggers logout/redirect-to-login without prop-drilling; (4) gate rendering in App.tsx/main.tsx behind auth state with a LoginScreen; (5) replace the hardcoded 'Omar H. / Operations' sidebar footer (App.tsx:82-88) with the real signed-in operator from context plus a Sign out action. All new UI reuses existing primitives (Button, Spinner, Avatar, the `.field-input`/`.field-label`/`.flash.error`/`.modal` CSS classes already in console.css) so no new styling system is needed.
steps: Define the backend contract this gate depends on (coordinate with backend auth workstream): POST /api/admin/login {email,password} -> 200 {token:string, operator:{id,name,email,role}} or 401; GET /api/admin/me with Authorization: Bearer <token> -> 200 {id,name,email,role} or 401; every /api/admin/* route returns 401 (not 403/500) on missing/invalid/expired bearer. Token is an opaque string (session id or signed JWT) — frontend treats it as opaque. Add a POST /api/admin/logout as optional (frontend can also just drop the token).

Create admin/src/lib/auth.ts: an Operator type {id,name,email,role}; in-memory `let token: string|null` plus localStorage persistence under a namespaced key (e.g. 'noor.admin.token'); functions getToken(), setToken(t)/persist, clearToken(); a registerOnUnauthorized(cb) hook storing a module-level callback that api.ts will invoke on 401; and async functions login(email,password) (POST /api/admin/login, store token, return operator) and fetchMe() (GET /api/admin/me). Keep these framework-agnostic so api.ts can import without a React cycle.

Refactor admin/src/lib/api.ts: in `get` (line 115) and `post` (line 128), build a headers object that always includes Authorization: `Bearer ${getToken()}` when a token exists; after `const res = await fetch(...)`, before the existing `if (!res.ok)` check, add `if (res.status === 401) { clearToken(); onUnauthorized?.(); throw new UnauthorizedError(); }`. Define and export a small `UnauthorizedError extends Error`. Apply the identical token-attach + 401 handling to the three loose fetch helpers createSession (line 168), initiateTransfer (line 178), fetchQrSvg (line 184) — factor a shared `authedFetch(url, init)` helper so the bearer/401 logic lives in exactly one place and both the /api/admin and /api/sessions calls use it.

Create admin/src/lib/AuthContext.tsx: an AuthProvider that on mount reads the persisted token; if present calls fetchMe() to validate+hydrate the operator (token may be expired); exposes {operator, status:'loading'|'authed'|'anon', login(email,password), logout()}. logout() clears the token and sets status anon. In a useEffect, call registerOnUnauthorized(() => { setStatus('anon'); setOperator(null) }) so a 401 from any in-flight request (api.ts) flips the whole app back to the login screen. Provide a useAuth() hook.

Create admin/src/pages/Login.tsx (LoginScreen): a centered card reusing .field-label/.field-input/.flash.error/Button(primary) classes; controlled email+password inputs; submit calls useAuth().login, shows inline error on failure (catch the thrown error message, same pattern as AddMerchantModal in Merchants.tsx:88-100) and a busy state on the Button. Mirror the existing brand glyph markup from App.tsx:66-73 for visual consistency.

Wire the gate in admin/src/main.tsx: wrap <App/> in <AuthProvider>. In App.tsx (or a thin Root component), read useAuth().status: 'loading' -> full-screen <Spinner/>; 'anon' -> <Login/>; 'authed' -> the existing console. This ensures no admin data is fetched (App.tsx:37-44 useEffect) until authenticated, since those calls would otherwise 401-loop on boot.

Replace the hardcoded operator footer in App.tsx:82-88 ('Omar H.' / 'Operations') with the real operator from useAuth(): <Avatar name={operator.name}/>, operator.name, operator.role, and add a Sign out control (a ghost Button or an icon-btn) that calls logout(). Optionally surface operator.email in a tooltip/title.

Make the existing settings/bell icon-btns (App.tsx:99-105) non-load-bearing or hide the bell's unread dot until backed; not required for auth but note that the topbar is where a logout menu could also live if preferred over the sidebar foot.

Confirm useAsync.ts needs no change: because api.ts now clears the token and triggers onUnauthorized on 401 (flipping the app to Login), the rejected promise's UnauthorizedError reaching useAsync.ts:17 is harmless (the page unmounts behind the Login screen). Optionally special-case UnauthorizedError in useAsync to suppress the red error flash during the redirect.

Update the TS Merchant interface note: api_key is currently declared on the Merchant interface (api.ts:44) and rendered nowhere, but the backend leak finding means once the backend returns a redacted MerchantResponse, drop api_key/ any secret fields from the TS interface so the console never holds a credential. This is a cross-workstream touchpoint, not blocking the gate itself.
depends_on: Backend admin authentication layer (POST /api/admin/login, GET /api/admin/me, Bearer enforcement + 401 on all /api/admin/* routes) — the [P0] 'Entire /api/admin/* surface is unauthenticated' finding. The frontend gate is cosmetic/defense-in-depth until the backend enforces auth and returns 401.
Backend redacted MerchantResponse DTO (the [P0] password_hash/api_key leak) so the SPA never receives secrets — needed before tightening the TS Merchant interface.
can_parallelize_with: Backend admin auth implementation can proceed in parallel against the agreed contract; integration happens at the /api/admin/login + /me boundary.
All other backend workstreams (session lifecycle CAS, MT webhook signature, ledger wiring, Plaid encryption) touch no files in admin/src and are fully independent.
designs.test_plan: "Manual: (1) with backend auth live, load /admin with no stored token -> Login screen renders, no /api/admin/* requests fire (verify in network tab — App's boot useEffect must not run). (2) Bad credentials -> inline error from login(), stays on Login. (3) Valid credentials -> token stored, console renders, sidebar footer shows the real operator name/role from /api/admin/me. (4) Reload page -> AuthProvider hydrates from localStorage via /api/admin/me, lands on console without re-login. (5) Force a 401 mid-session (e.g. delete the server-side session or hand-edit the localStorage token to garbage, then trigger a reload of any page) -> onUnauthorized fires, token cleared, app flips to Login without a raw error flash. (6) Sign out -> token cleared, Login screen, subsequent reload stays on Login. (7) Confirm every admin request carries Authorization: Bearer in the network tab, including the createSession/initiateTransfer/fetchQrSvg calls. Add a lightweight unit test (if a test runner is introduced) for auth.ts token persistence and the api.ts 401->UnauthorizedError path against a mocked fetch. Until the test runner exists (repo has zero tests), rely on `npm run build`/`tsc` in admin/ to catch type errors and manual verification."
designs.risk: "This is frontend-only and provides NO real security on its own — a token in localStorage and a client-side gate are trivially bypassed; the actual protection is the backend 401 enforcement, which is a hard dependency. If the backend ships before this, admin calls 401 and the console is unusable; if this ships before the backend, the gate is theater and the [P0] open-admin-surface remains. Token-in-localStorage is XSS-exfiltratable; prefer an httpOnly cookie session if the backend supports same-origin cookies (the SPA is served same-origin from /admin per router.rs:107-109, so cookie auth is viable and avoids the localStorage XSS risk) — flag this as a decision point with the backend workstream. The three loose fetch helpers hit the PUBLIC /api/sessions surface, not /api/admin; attaching an admin bearer there only helps once those routes also accept admin auth, otherwise the token is sent to endpoints that ignore it (low risk, but avoid leaking the admin token to unauthenticated public endpoints — scope the bearer attach to /api/admin/* and only send to session routes if the backend confirms it consumes admin auth there). No money-movement logic is touched."

designs.workstream: Compliance Roadmap: KYC/KYB, OFAC/AML, PCI/SOC2, Data Retention/Privacy, and Licensing Gates
designs.approach: This is a US bank-to-bank (ACH/RTP/FedNow/Wire) money-movement product with strong compliance SCAFFOLDING but no compliance FUNCTIONALITY. The merchants table already carries the KYB columns (business_type, registration_number, tax_id, industry_category, kyc_status TEXT DEFAULT 'not_started', risk_level, onboarding_completed_at, column_account_id) at migrations/001_initial_schema.sql:9-20, and the customer side has full identity/address/bank fields on payment_sessions (001:52-62). But NO flow populates or gates on any of it: admin create_merchant (admin_repo.rs ~176-209) inserts a merchant and lets kyc_status default to 'not_started'; update_merchant (admin_repo.rs ~216-247) only COALESCEs business_type/tax_id and never advances kyc_status; the seed (002_seed_data.sql:10,23) hardcodes status='active', kyc_status='verified' with zero checks; merchant_api.get_merchant_profile fakes {status:active,kyc_status:verified}; and confirm.rs:39-40 writes HARDCODED customer@example.com / 5555555555 as customer PII, corrupting the very identity data KYC depends on. There is no OFAC screening, no AML transaction monitoring, no sanctions list, no SAR/CTR workflow, no audit log, no data-retention or deletion path, and no license/bank-partner gate anywhere in crates/ (grep for ofac/sanction/aml/screen returns only field-name hits in models/repos). The product is also wide open (no auth on any route per router.rs:71-112), which is itself a compliance failure (GLBA Safeguards Rule, SOC 2 access control). This roadmap is delivered as a phased plan that explicitly tags each item CODE vs POLICY/BUSINESS, anchored to the existing schema so engineering can extend rather than rebuild. CRITICAL FRAMING: this platform CANNOT legally move money in production until the BUSINESS gate below is satisfied — either (a) a sponsor-bank / BaaS partner (e.g. Column is itself a chartered bank; Modern Treasury sits on partner banks) holds the regulatory perimeter and Depost operates as a Technology Service Provider / agent of the bank, OR (b) Depost obtains money-transmitter licenses in ~49 states + FinCEN MSB registration. Almost certainly (a). Every code item below is necessary but NOT sufficient without that gate. The remediation should reuse, not duplicate: extend the merchants table for KYB state, add screening/case tables, add an immutable audit-log table, wire screening calls into the existing confirm.rs counterparty step and the (to-be-built) merchant onboarding handler, and feed the existing-but-unused ledger + transactions tables into AML monitoring rules.
steps: BUSINESS/LEGAL GATE (P0, non-code, blocking): Determine the regulatory model. Given Column (a chartered bank) and Modern Treasury (bank-partner orchestration) are the rails, the intended model is almost certainly 'agent of a sponsor bank / BaaS', NOT direct money transmission. ACTION: (1) Execute a sponsor-bank or BaaS agreement that explicitly assigns the BSA/AML program ownership, names Depost's compliance obligations, and defines the bank's right to audit. (2) If any flow has Depost taking control of funds (holding balances, FBO accounts) outside a bank, obtain FinCEN MSB registration (31 CFR 1022.380) AND state money-transmitter licenses (NMLS) for every state of operation, plus surety bonds. (3) Designate a named BSA/AML Officer (regulatory requirement, an individual, not a role). (4) Stand up a written, board-approved BSA/AML Program (the '4 pillars', now 5 with CDD): internal controls, independent testing, designated officer, training, and ongoing CDD/risk. Until this gate is satisfied, production money movement is unlicensed and unlawful — gate the initiate endpoints behind a config flag that is false until legal sign-off.

KYB MERCHANT ONBOARDING FLOW (P0, mostly CODE + policy): There is currently NO onboarding flow — admin create_merchant just inserts a row. Build a state machine over the existing kyc_status column. POLICY: define required KYB data per business type (legal name, EIN/tax_id, registration_number, formation docs, beneficial owners >=25% per FinCEN CDD/beneficial-ownership rule, control person, business address, industry MCC, expected volume, website). CODE: (a) Add a migration introducing kyc_status as an explicit state machine with a CHECK constraint: ('not_started','documents_submitted','screening_pending','manual_review','verified','rejected','suspended'); (b) add tables merchant_kyb_documents (merchant_id FK, doc_type, storage_ref, uploaded_at, reviewed_by, decision) and merchant_beneficial_owners (merchant_id FK, full_name, dob, ssn_last4_encrypted, ownership_pct, address, screening_result); (c) add a POST /api/onboarding/* surface (authenticated as the merchant) that collects KYB data and transitions kyc_status='documents_submitted'; (d) only allow create_payment_link / create_session and initiate for a merchant whose kyc_status='verified' AND status='active' — add this check in merchant_api.rs and sessions.rs create paths (replacing the hardcoded DEMO_MERCHANT_ID); (e) set onboarding_completed_at on approval; (f) integrate the sponsor bank / KYB vendor (Middesk, Persona, or the bank's own KYC) call at the documents_submitted->screening_pending transition. CODE: also fix confirm.rs:39-40 to stop writing fake customer PII — accept real email/phone or COALESCE existing values, because customer identity feeds OFAC screening.

OFAC / SANCTIONS SCREENING (P0, CODE + policy): There is zero screening today. POLICY: screening obligation applies to BOTH merchants (and their beneficial owners/control persons at onboarding and on a rescreen cadence) AND the counterparty/customer on every payment (the person whose bank account is being credited/debited). CODE: (a) Add a sanctions_screenings table (subject_type ['merchant','beneficial_owner','counterparty'], subject_id, name, screened_at, provider, match_status ['clear','potential_match','confirmed_hit'], match_payload JSONB, decision, reviewed_by). (b) Integrate an OFAC SDN + consolidated-list screening provider (the sponsor bank usually mandates one — Sardine, ComplyAdvantage, or the bank's API; OFAC publishes the SDN list free for self-hosting as a fallback). (c) Wire screening into TWO points: at KYB onboarding (step 2) before kyc_status can reach 'verified', and into confirm.rs right before create_counterparty (confirm.rs:68) — screen req.customer_name + address; on potential_match, BLOCK the transition to Authorized and route to manual_review instead of proceeding. (d) Block initiate (sessions.rs:150, initiate.rs:13) if any unresolved screening hit exists for the session's counterparty. (e) Implement a rescreening job (sanctions lists change; rescreen all active merchants/owners on each SDN update, typically daily). POLICY: define the alert-adjudication SLA, the four-eyes review for clearing a potential match, and the blocking/reporting workflow on a confirmed hit (OFAC requires blocking the transaction and filing a blocked-property report within 10 business days).

AML TRANSACTION MONITORING + SAR/CTR (P0, CODE + heavy policy): No monitoring exists; the ledger and transactions tables are the data source but the ledger is never written (per audit) — AML monitoring depends on the ledger/settlement wiring landing first (depends_on). POLICY: write the AML monitoring rule set with the BSA/AML Officer and sponsor bank: structuring detection (multiple sub-$10k around the $10k CTR threshold), velocity/volume anomalies vs the merchant's stated expected volume captured at onboarding, high-risk geography, rapid in-out, dormant-then-active. Define CTR filing (FinCEN CTR for currency >$10k — narrow for pure bank-to-bank but required if applicable) and SAR filing (suspicious activity, 30-day filing clock, confidentiality). CODE: (a) Add tables aml_alerts (rule_id, merchant_id, session_id/transaction_id, severity, status ['open','investigating','closed_no_action','escalated_sar'], created_at) and aml_cases / sar_filings (case_id, narrative, filed_at, fincen_bsa_id). (b) Build a monitoring worker (tokio task spawned from main.rs alongside the webhook/expiry sweepers the audit recommends) that runs rules over settled transactions / ledger postings and opens aml_alerts. (c) Add a case-management UI in admin/ for analysts to investigate and disposition alerts. (d) Persist an immutable audit trail of every disposition. Recordkeeping: retain transaction records and SAR support for 5 years (BSA), screening evidence for the bank-defined period.

PCI DSS SCOPE & DATA PROTECTION (P1, CODE + policy): IMPORTANT scope note — this is ACH/bank-account movement, NOT card payments, so PCI DSS proper (which governs cardholder data / PANs) likely does NOT apply unless cards are ever accepted. The CONTROLLING regime here is the GLBA Safeguards Rule + NACHA's data-security rules for bank account/routing numbers, which the audit flagged are stored in PLAINTEXT (payment_sessions.customer_account_number/customer_routing_number TEXT, 001:60-61) and echoed to the browser (plaid.rs response). CODE: (a) Encrypt account/routing at rest via app-layer envelope encryption (KMS-managed DEK) or pgcrypto, or better, store only a provider token (Plaid processor_token / MT external_account_id) plus masked last-4 and never the raw PAN-equivalent; (b) remove raw numbers from all API responses and logs; (c) tokenize at the Plaid boundary. POLICY: document the data-flow / scope diagram, classify bank-account data as the sensitive tier, and if cards are ever added, isolate that flow to keep PCI scope minimal (SAQ-A via a hosted field). The wide-open API (no auth, router.rs) is also a PCI/GLBA control failure — see access-control item.

SOC 2 READINESS (P1, mostly POLICY + supporting CODE): SOC 2 (Trust Services Criteria: Security mandatory; Availability, Confidentiality, Processing Integrity relevant for payments) is a 6-12 month program. POLICY: establish the control environment — access-control policy, change-management (the repo has NO CI/CD per audit — add it), incident-response plan, vendor-risk management (MT/Column/Plaid are critical subprocessors), risk assessment, vulnerability management, and a formal SDLC. Engage an auditor for a Type I (point-in-time) then Type II (6-12 month observation) report. CODE prerequisites that directly map to SOC 2 criteria and are already gaps in this repo: (a) authentication/authorization on every route (today none — router.rs:71-112), the single largest Security-criterion failure; (b) an immutable, append-only audit_log table (actor, action, resource, before/after, ip, timestamp) covering all admin merchant mutations, KYC decisions, screening adjudications, and money-movement initiations — none exists today; (c) request tracing / structured logging (audit notes TraceLayer is compiled-in but never applied); (d) secrets management (audit found live-looking provider secrets committed in docker-compose.yml — rotate and move to a manager; this is a SOC 2 finding waiting to happen); (e) least-privilege DB and provider credentials. Processing Integrity ties directly to the ledger correctness and idempotency gaps the other workstreams own.

DATA RETENTION + GDPR/CCPA/GLBA PRIVACY (P1, CODE + policy): No retention or deletion logic exists; data lives forever in plaintext. POLICY: write a data-retention schedule reconciling competing obligations — BSA/AML mandates 5-year retention of transaction and CDD records (this OVERRIDES a consumer's GDPR/CCPA deletion request for transactional/AML data; deletion is deferred until the retention clock expires), while GLBA governs nonpublic personal information handling and the privacy notice. CCPA (California) and GDPR (if any EU data subjects) grant access/deletion/portability rights subject to the legal-hold exception. CODE: (a) Add a data-subject-request workflow (intake, identity verification, fulfillment) and a per-record retention/legal-hold flag; (b) implement scheduled purge jobs that delete or anonymize records past their retention window AND not under legal hold; (c) ensure PII (customer name, address, account numbers) is encrypted and access-logged so an access/portability request can be fulfilled accurately; (d) the confirm.rs hardcoded-PII bug (confirm.rs:39-40) must be fixed or every access request returns fabricated data. POLICY: publish a privacy policy + GLBA privacy notice, a record of processing activities (GDPR Art.30), and DPAs with MT/Column/Plaid as processors/subprocessors.

CROSS-CUTTING ENFORCEMENT GATE (P0, CODE): Tie compliance state to money movement. Because every route is currently unauthenticated and initiate moves money for any session UUID (router.rs:77-83), add a single hard gate: no create_session/create_payment_link unless the owning merchant is kyc_status='verified' AND status='active'; no confirm->Authorized unless customer OFAC screening is 'clear'; no initiate_transfer unless (merchant verified) AND (no open sanctions hit) AND (the global legal-go-live config flag is true). Persist the screening/decision references on the session so settlement reconciliation and audit can prove the controls ran. This single gate is the linchpin that makes the other items load-bearing rather than advisory.
depends_on: Auth & Security: authentication/authorization layer (every compliance gate is meaningless while all routes are unauthenticated; merchant identity must be resolvable, not DEMO_MERCHANT_ID)
Ledger & Balances: double-entry ledger + transactions wiring (AML transaction monitoring has no reliable data source until settlement actually writes ledger postings)
Plaid/Data: encryption/tokenization of bank account+routing numbers (GLBA/NACHA data-protection prerequisite for any production go-live)
Payment Lifecycle: distinct Failed/Returned/Reversed session states (AML/reconciliation and SAR evidence need true money-state, not Expired-for-everything)
can_parallelize_with: SOC 2 readiness policy work (mostly documentation, can proceed alongside code)
Data retention schedule + privacy policy drafting (policy)
Regulatory-model / sponsor-bank legal work (business track, runs in parallel with all engineering)
designs.test_plan: "There are ZERO tests in the workspace today (audit-confirmed), so this includes establishing the test harness. CODE items: (1) Unit tests for the kyc_status state machine — assert illegal transitions (e.g. not_started->verified without screening_pending) are rejected and the DB CHECK constraint holds. (2) Unit/integration tests that create_session/create_payment_link/initiate return 403 when the merchant is not kyc_status='verified'/status='active', and succeed when verified. (3) Mocked-HTTP tests for the OFAC screening client: 'clear' allows confirm->Authorized; 'potential_match' routes to manual_review and blocks; 'confirmed_hit' blocks initiate and creates a sanctions_screenings row with match_status='confirmed_hit'. (4) Test that confirm.rs persists the real customer email/phone (regression against the hardcoded customer@example.com / 5555555555). (5) AML monitor worker tests over seeded settled transactions: structuring and velocity rules open aml_alerts of expected severity. (6) Audit-log test: every admin merchant mutation and every initiate writes an immutable audit_log row (insert-only; assert UPDATE/DELETE are denied by grant or trigger). (7) Retention purge test: records past window and not under legal hold are purged; records under BSA 5-year hold are retained. POLICY items are validated by document review + auditor walkthrough, not automated tests. Pre-go-live: a tabletop test of the OFAC confirmed-hit blocking-and-reporting workflow and a SAR-filing dry run with the BSA/AML Officer."
designs.risk: "HIGHEST RISK is regulatory/legal, not technical: operating bank-to-bank money movement without the sponsor-bank agreement or money-transmitter licensing in place is unlicensed money transmission (potential criminal exposure under 18 USC 1960 and state law) and the missing OFAC screening means the platform could facilitate a transaction with a sanctioned party (strict-liability OFAC penalties). The unauthenticated API compounds this — anyone can currently trigger money movement and read all customer bank/PII (GLBA breach exposure). Technical risk in the remediation: the compliance gate must fail CLOSED (deny money movement on any screening/verification uncertainty or service outage), never fail open; a screening-provider outage must block, not bypass. Schema-migration risk: adding CHECK constraints to kyc_status will reject the seed's pre-set 'verified' demo merchants and any existing free-form values — backfill/normalize first. Retention-vs-deletion conflict: incorrectly honoring a GDPR/CCPA deletion request on BSA-retained records would itself be a BSA violation; the legal-hold exception must be enforced in code. Dependency risk: AML monitoring and ledger-based balances are only as trustworthy as the ledger wiring, which is currently entirely absent (audit-confirmed) — sequencing matters."

waves.rationale: Foundational, mostly-independent enablers that the rest of the program needs and that touch infra/config rather than the money-path handlers. Secrets rotation is an immediate emergency (live-format keys are in committed docker-compose.yml history). The typed Config / extended AppState{db,config,...} from CONFIG and SECRETS is a prerequisite for nearly every downstream stream (auth needs JWT_SECRET, PII needs the KEK, observability needs SENTRY_DSN/metrics handle, webhooks need per-provider secrets), so it must land first and the AppState struct shape must be agreed before other streams edit state.rs. The test base-URL refactor must land before contract tests can mock providers. These four edit largely disjoint files (Cargo.toml, main.rs, state.rs config plumbing, Dockerfile, .github/, provider base-URL constants, .sqlx/) but all three of CONFIG/SECRETS/TESTS touch the provider crate signatures and AppState/main.rs — coordinate the AppState definition and provider-fn signatures as a single agreed contract at the start of this wave to avoid churn.

parallel_workstreams: Authentication & Authorization (merchant API-key auth, admin JWT+roles, route nesting + middleware, redacted MerchantResponse, confirm_token session capability)
Observability & Audit Log (JSON tracing, request-ids, TraceLayer, Prometheus, Sentry, immutable audit_log table)
waves.rationale: Auth is the linchpin P0 that unblocks the compliance gate, the admin frontend gate, ledger/balance scoping, the webhook-retry endpoint, and IDOR closure — it should land as early as possible but AFTER the typed Config/AppState foundation (it adds config.jwt_secret and nests the router). Auth restructures router.rs and AppState and edits the money-path handlers (sessions.rs/confirm.rs to add the confirm_token gate, merchant_api.rs to drop DEMO_MERCHANT_ID), so it conflicts with the payment-core streams in Wave 2 and must be integrated before, not alongside, them. Observability runs concurrently with Auth: it adds the audit_log migration and threads an audit write through session_repo::update_status — which is the SAME chokepoint the lifecycle/CAS stream rewrites — so Observability's update_status touch must be coordinated with (ideally folded into) the Wave-2 lifecycle work; sequencing it to land its table/middleware here and its update_status audit hooks during Wave 2 avoids a double-rewrite. Both depend on Auth for the real actor_id (audit) and admin gating (metrics/retry), hence same wave with Auth slightly leading.

parallel_workstreams: Payment Session Lifecycle: SessionStatus terminal states (Failed/Returned/Reversed/Refunded) + state-machine CAS in update_status + collapse duplicate initiate endpoints + persist Expired/sweeper

Modern Treasury & Column provider hardening: thread Idempotency-Key + provider idempotency, error classification (definitive vs ambiguous), HTTP-status checks, FedNow/RTP rail correctness, persist active provider string
waves.rationale: This is the core of the coupled cluster. The lifecycle/CAS/state-machine work owns the rewrite of session_repo::update_status (the single transition chokepoint) and the SessionStatus enum in models.rs, and it collapses the two divergent initiate handlers — it MUST land before idempotency, failure-returns, and ledger because all of them depend on (a) the conditional CAS transition and (b) the distinct Failed/Returned/Reversed states. The provider-hardening stream lives in a separate crate (paybank-payments) and changes initiate_transfer/create_transfer signatures to accept an idempotency key and to expose an error-classification discriminant — both of which the lifecycle Err-path and the Wave-3 idempotency stream consume. These two can run together because the lifecycle stream edits the api crate's handlers/repo + models while provider hardening edits the payments crate; their only shared surface is the initiate_transfer call site and the error type, which they negotiate as the contract for Wave 3. Run them paired and integrate before Wave 3 opens.

parallel_workstreams: Idempotency wiring for money-movement endpoints (Idempotency-Key header contract, request-hash, two-transaction acquire+CAS pattern, deterministic reference, provider key propagation)

PII Protection (tokenize via Plaid processor_token / MT external_account_id, envelope-encrypt residual, drop plaintext columns, redact read paths) + Plaid bank-linking hardening (auth/ownership via confirm_token, status checks, propagate DB error, PLAID_ENV base URL)
waves.rationale: Idempotency depends on the Wave-2 lifecycle stream (its replay of a failed attempt must align with the new Failed terminal, not Expired) and the Wave-2 provider stream (it propagates the provider Idempotency-Key it just made available); it also depends on the refactor of session_repo + transaction_repo to a generic Transaction executor, which it shares with Ledger — so Idempotency and Ledger must not both rewrite create_transaction's signature simultaneously. PII/Plaid is grouped here because it depends on the Wave-0 KEK config and the Wave-1 auth (the confirm_token gate closes the Plaid exchange IDOR) and only shares confirm.rs with idempotency — a coordinated, narrow overlap. Idempotency edits sessions.rs/initiate.rs/confirm.rs/session_repo.rs/transaction_repo.rs heavily; PII edits confirm.rs/plaid.rs/session_repo.rs read+write paths — the session_repo.rs and confirm.rs overlap is the conflict to manage, so sequence the session_repo executor refactor (Idempotency owns it) before PII layers its encrypted-column changes on top.

parallel_workstreams: Ledger & Real Balances (per-merchant chart of accounts provisioning, double-entry postings in settlement path, verify_balance enforcement, real get_balance aggregation, DB money-safety constraints)
Failure / Returns / Reversals ledger entries (compensating reversal journals on Returned/Reversed/Refunded, idempotent on transfer_id)
waves.rationale: Ledger wiring depends on lifecycle states (Wave 2), the transaction_repo executor refactor (Wave 3 / shared), auth scoping for get_balance (Wave 1), and the idempotency/CAS settlement transaction it commits inside. The failure-returns ledger half is the natural companion: the forward settle journal (Ledger) must exist before the reversal journal (Failure-returns) has anything to mirror, so they pair in one wave with the settle path landing first. Both edit webhooks.rs settlement branches, initiate.rs/sessions.rs success paths, ledger_repo.rs, transaction_repo.rs, and add migration constraints — they must be co-developed to avoid double-posting (one pending entry at initiate, one posted-transition at settle, never two). Deferring ledger to here ensures it builds on the now-correct money-state machine and the atomic-transaction executor rather than racing them.

parallel_workstreams: Outbound Webhook Outbox + Delivery Worker (enqueue on transitions, SKIP-LOCKED claim, HMAC-signed delivery, backoff, admin retry endpoint + frontend wiring)
MT Webhook Signature Verification (HeaderMap + HMAC over raw body using configured MT secret, constant-time compare; align Column to constant-time + correct scheme)
waves.rationale: The outbound outbox depends on the lifecycle CAS (enqueue only on a real transition, gated on rowcount=1), the Failed/Returned/Reversed states (to derive payment.failed/returned/reversed events), the per-provider webhook secrets from Secrets, and the admin auth layer (the retry endpoint must sit behind admin auth). MT signature verification edits the same moderntreasury_webhook handler the lifecycle/ledger streams rewrote, so it lands after those settle to avoid conflicting edits, and it consumes the per-provider secret exposed by the Secrets/Config foundation. Pairing the two is natural since both finalize webhooks.rs. Although MT signature verification is a P0 forgery hole and ideally lands earliest, it touches the heavily-rewritten webhook handler — the pragmatic sequencing is to add the raw-body HMAC guard as the FIRST edit in this wave (it can technically be hoisted into Wave 1 as a standalone HeaderMap+verify wrapper if the team accepts re-integrating it after the handler rewrite); flagged as the one P0 that is sequencing-sensitive rather than truly late.

parallel_workstreams: Admin console auth gate (frontend: AuthContext, Login screen, bearer/credentials on api.ts, 401 redirect, real operator footer, drop api_key from TS Merchant)

Compliance Roadmap CODE items (kyc_status state machine + CHECK, KYB onboarding flow, OFAC screening wired into confirm + initiate gate, AML monitoring worker, audit-log enforcement, retention purge, fail-closed compliance gate)
waves.rationale: The admin frontend gate is purely admin/src and depends only on the backend admin-auth contract (Wave 1) being live; it provides no security on its own (the backend 401 enforcement is the real control) so it lands after auth. Compliance CODE depends on auth (resolvable merchant identity, not DEMO_MERCHANT_ID), the ledger (AML monitoring has no data source until settlement writes postings — Wave 4), PII encryption (GLBA/NACHA prerequisite — Wave 3), and the distinct failure states (SAR/reconciliation evidence — Wave 2), so it is necessarily last among code work. Both run concurrently here because they touch disjoint surfaces (admin/src vs new compliance crates/migrations + the existing confirm/initiate gate). NOTE: the Compliance POLICY/BUSINESS track (sponsor-bank agreement, MSB/MTL licensing, BSA/AML Officer, SOC2 program, privacy/retention docs) is NOT a wave dependency — it runs in parallel from Wave 0 onward as a separate legal/policy stream and is the true production go-live gate; the fail-closed config flag on initiate stays false until that legal sign-off, regardless of code completion.
